DocsHome.title: Connex documentation
DocsHome.lead: Connex is a relationship-intelligence CRM: it scores how warm each relationship is, predicts when one is cooling, and surfaces the warmest path to any introduction. These docs walk every capability, from the big fundamentals down to the small interface details.

DocsGettingStarted.title: Getting started
DocsGettingStarted.description: What Connex is, how workspaces work, and how to find your way around.
DocsGettingStarted.lead: Start here. These pages cover the mental model behind Connex and the fundamentals every other section builds on.

what-is-connex.title: What is Connex
what-is-connex.description: The relationship-intelligence CRM and the ideas that make it different.

text: Connex is a CRM built around one simple idea: your relationships have a temperature, and that temperature changes over time. Instead of leaving your contacts as a flat, static list, Connex quietly keeps track of how warm each relationship is, gives you a heads-up when one is starting to cool, and shows you the friendliest way to reach anyone you want to meet.
Everything you do lives inside your own workspace, and what you can see, edit, and share follows your role on the team. You are always working in your own space, with your own people.

blocks.text: What makes it different

items.title: Warmth scoring
items.description: Every relationship gets a simple warmth score, based on how recently and how often you connect and how deep the relationship runs.

items.title: Cooling alerts
items.description: Connex tells you when a warm relationship is about to go cold, so you can reach out before it slips away.

items.title: Warm introductions
items.description: Want to meet someone new? Connex finds the strongest chain of people who can introduce you.

items.title: Job history
items.description: People keep their work history, so when a contact changes companies you never lose the relationship you built.

blocks.title: Read in any order
blocks.body: Each article stands on its own. But Getting started and Core concepts give you the handful of words the rest of the docs lean on, so they are a good place to begin.

workspaces-and-tenancy.title: Workspaces and teams
workspaces-and-tenancy.description: How workspaces keep each team's data separate, and how to switch between them.

blocks.text: A workspace is your own private space in Connex. Every record, file, tag, and setting lives inside one workspace, and nothing ever crosses from one to another. You can belong to more than one workspace, say for different teams or clients, and switch between them anytime without logging out.

items.title: Open the workspace switcher
items.description: It sits at the top of the sidebar and shows the workspace you are in right now.

items.title: Pick another workspace
items.description: The whole app switches over instantly, showing only the people and records from that workspace.

items.title: Pick up where you left off
items.description: Connex remembers your choice, so next time you land back in the same workspace.

blocks.title: Your data stays private
blocks.body: Your information never leaks between workspaces. The only way someone in another workspace sees your work is if you invite them or share a record with them on purpose.

navigating-connex.title: Navigating Connex
navigating-connex.description: The sidebar, global search, breadcrumbs, and how the app is laid out.

blocks.text: The sidebar on the left splits Connex into a few clear areas: Overview, Records, Marketing (when campaigns are enabled), Activity, Library, Workspace, and Help & resources. The bar across the top holds search, along with a button to hide or show the sidebar. The workspace you are in is shown at the top of the sidebar itself. On most detail pages a back button takes you straight to the list you came from.

items.action: Close the open menu or dialog

blocks.title: Search is your fastest route
blocks.body: Whenever you are not sure where something lives, just start typing in search. It reaches across your people, companies, and records, so you rarely need to click through the menus.

core-concepts.title: Core concepts
core-concepts.description: Records, relationships, signals, and the shared table mechanics.

blocks.text: A few words come up again and again in Connex. Learn them once and every other page gets easier to follow.

blocks.title: Words worth knowing

Any interaction, like an email or a meeting, that adds to a relationship's warmth.
A saved group of records that matches rules you set, so it stays up to date on its own.
A warm connection you ask for, passed along through someone you both know.

items.question: Is my data shared across workspaces?
items.answer: No. Each record belongs to one workspace and never shows up in another.

items.question: Do I have to score relationships myself?
items.answer: No. Connex works out the warmth for you, from the interactions it already keeps track of.

quickstart.title: Quickstart
quickstart.description: Go from an empty workspace to your first tracked relationship in about five minutes.

blocks.text: This is your first five minutes with Connex. In a few quick steps you will sign in, add your first company and contact, log one interaction, and watch a warmth reading appear on the relationship. By the end you will have a living record instead of an empty workspace, and you will know the loop that keeps every relationship warm.

blocks.name: contact-card
blocks.caption: A contact in Connex: their details, work history, and warmth reading all in one place.

items.title: Sign in and land on your dashboard
items.description: Sign in and Connex drops you on your dashboard, your home base. It is quiet at first, which is exactly what we are about to fix. If you belong to more than one workspace, check that the right one is selected in the workspace switcher at the top of the sidebar.

items.title: Add your first company
items.description: Head to Records and create a company, the organization you do business with. Give it a name to start. A company gathers its people, deals, and a history of your interactions all in one place.

items.title: Add a contact and link it to the company
items.description: Now add a contact, a real person you know, and connect them to the company you just made. Their name and email are plenty to begin. Everything else can come later.

items.title: Log one interaction
items.description: Open your new contact and jot a quick note about your last conversation, or log an activity like a call or a meeting. This is the signal Connex learns from, so even a short line counts.

items.title: See the warmth appear
items.description: That single interaction gives the relationship a warmth reading, shown as one of four bands from hot to cold. You never set it by hand. Keep logging as you work and it stays current on its own.

blocks.title: The habit that makes Connex shine
blocks.body: The more of your real interactions you log, notes, calls, meetings, the smarter Connex gets about which relationships are thriving and which are cooling off. You do not have to score anything yourself. Just keep working normally and let the warmth keep itself up to date.

items.question: Do I have to set the warmth score myself?
items.answer: No. Connex works out the temperature for you from the notes, activities, and meetings you already log. There is nothing to fill in by hand.

items.question: Where does everything I add live?
items.answer: Inside your workspace, and it stays private to it. What you can view and edit follows your role on the team.

DocsDashboard.title: Dashboard & home
DocsDashboard.description: Your personalized home: greeting, at-a-glance metrics, and what needs attention.
DocsDashboard.lead: The dashboard is the first thing you see. It summarizes your workspace and points you at what is urgent.

home-dashboard.title: The home dashboard
home-dashboard.description: Greeting, overview cards, cooling relationships, tasks, and recent moves.

text: The dashboard is your home in Connex, and the first thing you see when you sign in. It greets you by name and shows today's date, so you land somewhere familiar every time.

Right at the top, a short status line tells you whether anything needs you. If you have overdue tasks, it turns red and shows the count. If things are simply coming up this week, like deals closing or tasks due, it gives you a calm summary. And when nothing is pressing, it happily says so.

blocks.name: dashboard-overview
blocks.caption: Your workspace at a glance

items.title: Four key totals
items.description: See your current count of companies, contacts, deals, and pipelines, each on its own card.

items.title: Tap any card to dig in
items.description: Every card and nearly every row is a link. Click through to jump straight to the records behind the number.

items.title: Always the current count
items.description: The totals are read from your workspace every time the dashboard loads, so they match what the records pages show.

items.title: See where your pipeline is heading
items.description: A chart plots twelve months of pipeline, blending recent history with a forecast. Switch between money already earned from closed deals and the projected value of your open ones.

items.title: Work in more than one currency
items.description: If your deals span currencies, pick which one to view. It starts on your most common currency and shows how many deals sit in each.

items.title: Know what's on your plate
items.description: See your open tasks, anything overdue, what's due this week, and your next few tasks with their dates. Overdue ones stand out in red so nothing slips.

items.title: Check tasks off right here
items.description: Tick a task complete without leaving the dashboard. It updates instantly, and if you change your mind, a quick undo is one click away.

items.title: Relationships that are cooling off
items.description: See contacts who were once warm but have gone quiet, most dormant first, with their company and how warm the relationship still is.

items.title: Follow up in one click
items.description: Schedule a follow-up before a contact goes cold, right from the dashboard. The task lands on your list and links back to that person.

items.title: People who just changed jobs
items.description: Spot contacts who moved to a new company, with their old company, their new one, and when the move happened. A perfect reason to reach out.

items.title: Introductions you could make
items.description: Get suggestions of people worth introducing to each other, along with why, like a shared employer or mutual connections.

items.title: Your recent files
items.description: The latest files you have added, with their type and date, plus a running total of how much storage you have used. Click any file to open it.

items.title: A feed of what's happened
items.description: Recent tasks, activities, and notes gathered into one timeline, so you can see who did what and which records were involved.

blocks.title: Start your day here
blocks.body: Glance at the status line and the cooling-relationships list first thing each morning. Between the two, you'll know exactly who needs a nudge and what's due, before you open anything else.

items.question: Why does a section show a message instead of a list?
items.answer: When there's nothing to show yet, sections like cooling relationships, recent moves, and files display a short note instead of empty space. They'll fill in as you use Connex.

items.question: When is a follow-up scheduled for?
items.answer: Connex aims to catch a contact before they cool off. If it can predict when a relationship will go cold, it schedules your follow-up a few days ahead of that, and never earlier than tomorrow.

items.question: Does the dashboard fit my language and screen?
items.answer: Yes. Everything follows your language, English or Japanese, and the layout rearranges to fit your screen, from a wide desktop down to a narrow window.

records-overview.title: Records overview
records-overview.description: How the four record types relate and what they have in common.

text: Records are the people and organizations you keep track of in Connex. There are four kinds: companies, contacts, deals, and pipelines. They all look and work the same way, so once you learn one, the rest feel familiar.
Everything lives inside your workspace and stays private to it. What you can view, edit, or delete depends on your role.

companies.title: Companies
companies.description: Organizations, their people, deals, custom fields, and timeline.

blocks.text: A company is an organization you do business with. Connex keeps all your companies in one place, which you can view as cards or as a table, and search by name, website, industry, phone, or address. Open any company to see its full profile.

items.title: Fill in the basics
items.description: Enter the name, website, industry, phone, and address. Drop in a logo if you have one. If you don't, Connex shows a nice lettered avatar instead.

items.title: Let the helpers do the work
items.description: The industry field suggests values you already use, and the website field tidies up the web address for you.

items.title: Line up its people
items.description: Add one or more contacts, each with a name, title, email, and photo, to be created alongside the company.

items.title: Save
items.description: The company is created first, then its people. If some people can't be added, Connex tells you how many went through.

blocks.title: We catch duplicate companies
blocks.body: If the website you enter already belongs to another company, Connex shows a warning that links you to that company and stops the save. That way you never end up with two records for the same business.

items.title: Its people
items.description: Everyone who works at the company, with a quick button to add someone new.

items.title: Deals & pipeline
items.description: The company's deals grouped by stage, with names, values, and status.

items.title: Revenue
items.description: Closed and projected revenue, shown clearly in the company's main currency.

items.title: Engagement chart
items.description: A 12-week view of how often you've been in touch, with a per-week breakdown on hover.

items.title: Timeline
items.description: Every activity, note, and task for the company and its people, in order.

items.title: Your team
items.description: See which teammates have worked with this company, and jump to their profiles.

blocks.title: Jump to companies in the same industry
blocks.body: The industry on a company profile is a link. Click it to instantly see every other company in that same industry.

items.question: How is a company's warmth worked out?
items.answer: It's based on how recently and how often you've been in touch with the company's people. Older contact counts for less over time, so the score stays current. You can sort your companies by it.

items.question: Can I edit or delete several companies at once?
items.answer: Yes. Select a few and edit shared details together, or delete them in one step. Connex confirms first and tells you the result for each one.

items.question: Does Connex remember how I like to view things?
items.answer: Yes. Your card-or-table choice is remembered after a refresh, and you can save full filter setups as named views to reuse anytime.

contacts.title: Contacts
contacts.description: People, their employment history, warmth, and connections.

blocks.text: A contact is a person you know. Each one has a profile with their name, email, phone, title, company, tags, and photo, plus the relationship context Connex is built around: their work history, a warmth score, their connections into your network, and a full activity timeline.

blocks.caption: A contact profile, with warmth and tags

items.title: Start with a name

items.title: Add a photo

items.title: Save
items.description: A quick success animation confirms it, and the dialog closes.

items.title: Edit anytime, one or many
items.description: Update a single contact, or edit the name, email, phone, and title across several at once. Deleting always asks you to confirm first.

items.title: Identity

items.title: Work history

items.title: Warmth

items.title: Connections

items.title: Activity timeline
items.description: Activities, notes, and tasks in one dated feed, showing who added each.

items.title: Deals
items.description: The deals this person is part of, with status, name, and value.

items.title: Log activity
items.description: Record a call, email, meeting, or note, with a subject and an optional deal.

items.title: Notes & tasks
items.description: Jot a note, or create a task with an owner and due date.

items.title: Tags
items.description: Add color-coded tags to one contact, or to many at once.

items.title: Custom fields
items.description: Fill in your workspace's extra fields right on the profile.

items.title: Attachments

items.title: At-a-glance stats
items.description: Cards count activities, open tasks, and deals, and show which teammates have engaged.

blocks.title: Quick actions on a contact
rows: Opens a new message to their address.
Copies the phone number and confirms it for you.
Reassigns or clears their company, and notes the move in their work history.
Opens the map focused on this contact.
Shares the contact with teammates in your workspace.

items.question: Does work history keep itself up to date?
items.answer: Yes. Whenever you add a contact or change their company, on their own or in a batch, Connex records the move for you and marks the current role.

items.question: Can I find people who just changed jobs?
items.answer: Yes. Connex keeps a 'recently moved' feed of contacts who changed companies recently, so you can reach out at the right moment.

items.question: What does the warm-intro path show?
items.answer: It's the shortest chain of people you know that reaches someone you'd like to meet. It also tells you when you already know them directly, or when there's no path to them right now.

deals-and-pipelines.title: Deals & pipelines
deals-and-pipelines.description: Opportunities moving through stages, and the pipelines that shape them.

blocks.text: A deal is an opportunity moving through a pipeline. It has a name, value, currency, company, owner, and stage, and ends as either won or lost. A pipeline is the set of stages a deal moves through. Both live in your workspace, and roles decide who can change them.

blocks.name: pipeline-board
blocks.caption: Deals moving through pipeline stages

items.title: See all your pipelines
items.description: Each pipeline shows its stages, how many deals are in it, and who's involved.

items.title: Create and adjust
items.description: Name a pipeline, give it stages, and rename, add, or remove them anytime.

items.title: Winning and losing stages
items.description: Mark a stage as won or lost. When a deal reaches one, it closes with that outcome automatically.

items.title: Progress at a glance
items.description: A deal's page shows a timeline of its stages, with the current one highlighted and whether it's on schedule.

blocks.title: A few stage rules Connex looks after
body: Each pipeline can have one winning stage and one losing stage.
A deal can only move between stages in its own pipeline.
Reopen a closed deal and it slides back to the last open stage, with its close date and outcome tidied up for you.

items.title: Create and quick-edit
items.description: Add a deal with helpful checks as you type, and edit one or many at a time.

items.title: Team
items.description: Give the deal one owner and as many collaborators as you like.

items.title: People
items.description: Link the contacts involved, each with the role they play in the deal.

items.title: Tags & custom fields
items.description: Organize with color-coded tags and fill in your workspace's extra fields.

items.title: Timeline
items.description: Activities, notes, tasks, and key moments like stage changes, all in one feed.

items.title: Attachments
items.description: Keep proposals, contracts, and other files right on the deal.

blocks.text: When a deal is done, mark it won or lost to record the outcome, an optional reason, and the value you actually landed. The close date is filled in for you, and reopening clears it again. For closed deals, Connex shows how the final value compared to what you projected, and status pills read open, won, or lost at a glance. Your expected and actual close dates tell you whether a deal is on time, ahead, behind, or overdue.

items.title: Revenue forecast
items.description: A chart pairing the last six months with the six ahead, projected value against what actually closed.

items.title: Stage and pipeline mix
items.description: See how your deals and revenue spread across stages and pipelines at a glance.

items.title: Key totals
items.description: Summary tiles for your open pipeline value, the number of open deals, closed forecast, and closed revenue.

items.title: Forecast accuracy
items.description: See how your actual closed revenue compared with what you forecast, shown as a percentage.

items.question: How does working in different currencies work?
items.answer: Each deal has its own currency, so values show the right symbol and formatting. You can filter by currency, and charts add up one currency at a time so nothing gets mixed together.

items.question: What happens when I move a deal to a won or lost stage?
items.answer: It closes on its own with that outcome. If the deal was already closed, its outcome updates to match the new stage.

items.question: Who can change deals and pipelines?
items.answer: That's set by roles and permissions: creating, editing, closing, deleting deals, and managing pipelines are each their own permission. Deletions ask you to confirm, and every change is kept in a complete, unchangeable history.

table-and-grid.title: Table & grid mechanics
table-and-grid.description: Sorting, column controls, selection, and bulk actions shared across records.

blocks.text: Companies, contacts, deals, and pipelines all use the same table and grid, so whatever you learn here works everywhere records are listed. View any list as cards or as a table, and Connex remembers your choice for each kind of record.

items.title: Card grid
items.description: A flexible grid of cards you can click and select, each with an avatar, a summary, and an actions menu.

items.title: Data table
items.description: A compact table with sortable columns and a checkbox for each row.

items.title: Always in view
items.description: The name columns stay fixed as you scroll sideways, so you never lose track of which record you're looking at.

items.title: Your choice sticks
items.description: Your card-or-table preference is remembered across reloads.

items.title: Column sorting
items.description: Click a column header to sort, and click again to flip the direction.

items.title: Search
items.description: Type to search the record's key fields and see matches right away.

items.title: Filters
items.description: Narrow the list with filters built from your own data, and see how many are active at a glance.

items.title: Filter chips
items.description: Active filters and your search show up as chips you can remove with a click.

items.title: Saved views
items.description: Save a full setup of filters, sort, and search under a name. A dot shows when there are unsaved changes.

items.description: Build sharper lists by combining ideas like 'warm intro' or 'open deal' with your own conditions.

items.title: Select rows
items.description: Tick individual checkboxes, or the one in the header to select every record in the current list, across all its pages.

items.title: Use the selection bar
items.description: A floating bar shows how many you've selected and what you can do with them.

items.title: Apply an action
items.description: Add or remove a tag, reassign an owner, change a deal's stage, edit shared fields, or delete. Connex reports the result for each one.

blocks.title: Edit and move data in place

items.description: A side panel edits shared fields across everything you've selected, all at once.

items.title: Inline custom fields
items.description: Edit custom-field cells right in the table. Double-click or press Enter to start.

items.title: Custom field columns

items.title: Copyable cells

items.title: Import and export

items.title: Open a record
items.description: Click a row or card to open its full page. Clicks on checkboxes, copy cells, and menus won't navigate away.

blocks.title: Getting around a wide table
blocks.body: When a table has more columns than fit, soft shading at the edges hints there's more to see, and you can drag the header to scroll sideways. The name columns stay in view the whole way across, so you always know which record you're looking at.

items.question: How many records show per page?
items.answer: 25 by default, and you can switch to 10, 25, 50, or 100. A 'Showing X to Y of Z' line keeps you oriented.

items.question: Do my edits show up right away?
items.answer: Yes. Quick edits, custom-field changes, and bulk actions update on screen instantly, and gently undo with a message if something doesn't go through.

items.question: What do I see while things load or when nothing matches?
items.answer: While a list loads you'll see placeholder shapes, and when nothing matches you'll get a friendly empty state with a Clear Filters button when filters are on.

products-and-line-items.title: Products & line items
products-and-line-items.description: A catalogue of what you sell, and how line items decide a deal's value.

text: The product catalogue is the list of things you sell. Adding them to a deal as line items builds up the deal's value from real numbers instead of a figure someone typed from memory.
You will find the catalogue under Records, and line items on the deal itself.

blocks.name: deal-line-items
blocks.caption: With line items on a deal, the deal value is the sum of the lines rather than a typed figure.

items.title: What a product holds
items.description: A name, an optional code, a unit and unit price, a currency, an optional tax rate, and whether it is charged once or repeats.

items.title: Administrators maintain it
items.description: Everyone can see the catalogue and use it on deals, but creating, editing and deleting products is an administrator permission.

items.title: Retire rather than delete
items.description: Marking a product inactive removes it from the picker on deals while leaving it in the catalogue. Deleting it is permanent, but never disturbs deals that already use it.

items.title: Export, but no import
items.description: You can export the catalogue to CSV. There is no product import, so a large catalogue has to be entered through the interface.

blocks.text: When you add a product to a deal, Connex copies its details onto the line at that moment. Changing the catalogue afterwards never reaches back into deals that already quoted the old price, which is what makes an old deal still readable a year later.

blocks.title: How a deal's value is decided
rows: Whatever you type in. This is the normal case for a deal you are sizing early.
The sum of the lines, recalculated every time you add, change or remove one. Typing over it is refused.
You remove the last line item
Back under your control, keeping the last calculated figure rather than resetting to zero.
The calculated total becomes the realised value and is frozen there, so later edits move the deal value but never the revenue you booked.

The realised value is set to zero when you lose the deal through the close dialog. Other routes to a lost stage do not currently clear a realised value that was already recorded, so a deal won and later marked lost can keep its won figure; this is a known defect rather than the intended contract.

blocks.title: One currency per deal, and no conversion
blocks.body: A deal and all of its line items share a single currency. A product priced in a different currency cannot be added, and the currency cannot be changed while line items exist. Connex never converts between currencies, so totals across your workspace are always reported per currency and never added together.

blocks.title: Repeating charges are counted once
blocks.body: A repeating line contributes its amount for a single period, and the deal value is the one-off charges plus that. It is what you booked, not an annual or full-contract figure, and Connex does not multiply it out by a term.

items.question: Can I apply a discount to a line?
items.answer: Discounts are shown on a line and included in its total, but there is no discount field to fill in on the deal screen. Set the price you mean on the line, or price the product accordingly in the catalogue.

items.question: Our historical deal values changed. Why?
items.answer: When derived values were introduced, every deal that already had line items had its value recalculated from those lines. That is a one-off correction, and the new figures are the ones that agree with the lines.

items.question: Someone deleted a product we had quoted. Did we lose the quote?
items.answer: No. The line keeps its own copy of the name, price and tax, so the deal and any document generated from it are unaffected.

items.title: Deals and pipelines

DocsRelationshipIntelligence.title: Relationship intelligence
DocsRelationshipIntelligence.description: Warmth scoring, decay prediction, connections, and employment history: the heart of Connex.
DocsRelationshipIntelligence.lead: This is what sets Connex apart. Relationships are scored, watched for decay, and mapped into a graph you can traverse.

warmth-and-temperature.title: Warmth & temperature
warmth-and-temperature.description: How relationship temperature is scored and what the bands mean.

blocks.text: Ever wish you could glance at your contacts and instantly know which relationships are thriving and which need a little love? That is exactly what temperature does. Every relationship in Connex carries a warmth reading that goes up when you are in regular, meaningful contact and drifts down when things go quiet. It rolls up into four simple bands, so you can scan a whole list and know where you stand at a glance.

blocks.name: warmth-scale
blocks.caption: The four warmth bands, from hot to cold

items.label: Hot
items.description: You are in frequent, recent contact. This relationship is thriving.

items.label: Warm
items.description: Healthy and current. You stay in touch steadily, just less often.

items.label: Cool
items.description: Starting to fade. Things have slowed down, so it is a good time to reach out.

items.label: Cold
items.description: Gone quiet. There has been little recent contact to build on.

blocks.title: You never set this by hand
blocks.body: There is nothing to fill in. Connex works out the temperature for you from the things you already track: your notes, activities, meetings, and tasks. Just keep working normally and the score keeps itself current.

blocks.title: Use it to plan your day
blocks.body: Sort your people by warmth and start with the ones cooling off. A quick check-in at the right moment is often all it takes to keep a good relationship warm.

decay-and-signals.title: Decay & signals
decay-and-signals.description: How Connex predicts cooling relationships and what feeds the score.

blocks.text: Good relationships fade if you leave them alone too long, and it is easy to lose track of who you have not spoken to in a while. Connex watches for that quiet drift and gives you a heads-up before a relationship cools, so you can reach out while it still feels natural. You will find these flagged on your dashboard as cooling relationships.

items.title: Notes
items.description: Any context you jot down about a person or company.

items.title: Activities
items.description: Calls, meetings, and other touchpoints you log.

items.title: Tasks
items.description: Follow-ups you complete for that relationship.

items.title: Calendar events
items.description: Meetings connected to the people involved.

blocks.title: Reach out before the reminder feels overdue
blocks.body: A cooling flag is a nudge, not a scolding. Acting on it early, with a short message or a quick call, is usually enough to bring the warmth right back up.

connections-and-employment.title: Connections & employment
connections-and-employment.description: The relationship graph and how job history keeps context when people move.

blocks.text: People change jobs, and when they do you do not want to lose everything you know about them. In Connex, people are linked to the companies they work at through their job history. So when a contact moves on, your relationship and all its context move with them, and your view of who works where stays up to date automatically.

items.title: Nothing gets lost when people move
items.description: A contact who switches companies keeps their full history with you, so you never start from scratch.

items.title: New doors open up
items.description: Someone you already know landing at a company you are chasing can become your warmest way in.

items.title: Warm-intro paths

items.title: Relationship map
items.description: See how everyone connects, laid out visually for you to explore.

ai-insights.title: AI insights
ai-insights.description: What the optional AI features write, what grounds them, and what leaves your workspace.

text: Connex can use an AI model to explain what it already knows. It writes a short brief on a deal, says why a deal looks at risk, says why an introduction is worth making, drafts the summary at the top of a report, and reads a business card when the built-in reader cannot.
Everything AI writes sits on top of figures Connex computed itself. The numbers, risk factors and warmth scores are never produced by a model, and they remain the authority if the two ever disagree.

blocks.title: AI is off until someone turns it on
blocks.body: AI is switched off for the whole instance by default. Your organisation also has to connect its own AI provider, and the permission to use AI is given to administrators rather than ordinary members by default. Until all three line up, the AI panels simply do not appear, which is the expected state rather than a fault.

items.title: A brief has to cite what it used
items.description: Every section names the records it drew on, and the citations are checked against the records that were actually supplied. A brief that cites something it was not given is discarded rather than shown.

items.title: It refuses when there is too little to go on
items.description: If a deal has almost no history, Connex says there is not enough activity yet to write a reliable brief instead of producing something confident and empty.

items.title: It admits when it was working blind
items.description: If part of the surrounding context could not be gathered, the brief says so underneath rather than quietly leaving it out.

items.title: Explanations are tied to the real signals
items.description: The risk write-up may only refer to the risk factors Connex actually calculated for that deal, and an introduction write-up only to the reasons behind that suggestion. Anything else is rejected.

blocks.text: Every AI panel is stamped with the date and time it was generated, so you can tell a fresh reading from one written weeks ago. Results are reused when nothing relevant has changed, and you can ask for a fresh one.

items.title: Names and contact details are replaced first
items.description: People, companies, email addresses and phone numbers are swapped for placeholders before anything is sent, and swapped back in the answer. In free text, Connex additionally removes email addresses, web addresses and long runs of digits such as phone numbers. It does not detect postal addresses in free text, so a street address typed into a note is sent as written.

items.title: Sensitive free text is withheld, not masked
items.description: Text that looks like it might touch a specially protected category is left out of the request entirely rather than being sent in a disguised form. Connex errs towards withholding too much.

items.title: A final check runs before anything is sent
items.description: The exact outgoing request is inspected for any raw identifier that should have been replaced. If one is found the request is abandoned and recorded, rather than sent.

items.title: Only metadata is recorded
items.description: The audit trail keeps which feature ran, which provider and model, and whether it succeeded. It never stores the text sent or the text returned.

blocks.title: Two honest limits
blocks.body: Replacing identifiers reduces what your AI provider sees, but Connex still holds the mapping and can read the result, so this is not anonymisation. And an image cannot be masked at all, so a business card sent to a provider goes as the picture it is.

items.title: The built-in reader goes first
items.description: Where card reading is available on your instance it is used first, and nothing leaves your deployment. A provider is only involved if that reader is unavailable.

items.title: You are told which fields came from AI
items.description: Fields filled by a provider are named for you to check, and are shown without the confidence figures that accompany the built-in reader. Nothing is saved until you confirm it.

items.question: Why did an AI panel say it is temporarily unavailable?
items.answer: There is a limit on how many generations an organisation can run in a short window, so that one busy person cannot exhaust it for everyone. Wait a moment and try again.

items.question: Can I stop a particular contact being sent to an AI provider?
items.answer: Yes. Restricting processing for a contact excludes them from AI features and clears anything already generated that involved them.

items.question: Does it write in Japanese?
items.answer: Connex asks the model to answer in your language, and the interface around it is fully translated. The wording itself comes from your provider's model, so treat the language of the answer as a strong request rather than a guarantee.

DocsOverviewSuite.title: Overview suite
DocsOverviewSuite.description: Analytics, the relationship map, calendar, introductions, and warm-intro paths.
DocsOverviewSuite.lead: The overview suite turns your records into insight: charts, a live relationship graph, and tools for engineering introductions.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.description: Revenue trends, pipeline value, win rates, and team leaderboards.

blocks.text: The analytics dashboard brings your deals, pipelines, and team activity together on one screen, so you can see how the business is doing at a glance: revenue, pipeline health, win rates, and where deals are getting stuck. It's one of the overview pages in Connex, reached from the sidebar, alongside the map, calendar, and introductions.

items.title: Time range
items.description: Look at the last 30 days, 90 days, or 12 months. Everything on the page updates to match.

items.title: Currency
items.description: If your deals span several currencies, pick the one to show everything in. Connex starts you on your most-used currency.

items.title: Won revenue
items.description: The real money you closed in this period, based on each deal's final value.

items.title: New pipeline
items.description: The total value of every deal that opened in this period, whether or not it later closed.

items.title: Win rate
items.description: Of the deals that closed, the share you won. Deals closed without a clear won or lost outcome are left out.

items.title: Average sales cycle
items.description: How long a typical deal takes, from opening to closing a win. Lower is faster.

items.title: Revenue trend
items.description: Money won each month, next to what your pipeline could bring in ahead.

items.title: Pipeline value
items.description: Your pipelines ranked by total value, so you can see where the weight sits.

items.title: Stage funnel
items.description: Open deals in a pipeline, broken down by stage, so you can spot where deals pile up.

items.title: Win rate donut
items.description: Won versus lost at a glance, with your win rate in the middle.

items.title: Activity volume
items.description: How much your team is logging over time, split by type.

items.title: Team leaderboard
items.description: Your five most active people, counting activities, tasks, and notes together.

items.title: Deal aging
items.description: Which open deals are fresh and which are going stale, so nothing slips.

items.title: Top deals
items.description: Your three biggest open deals and three biggest wins, ready to click into.

blocks.title: Reading the trends
blocks.body: Each headline number carries a small trend line and an arrow comparing this period to the one before. Green means it moved in a good direction, red means it's worth a look. When there's nothing to compare against yet, you'll see 'No prior data' instead of a misleading figure.

items.question: Why is a pipeline already picked in the funnel?
items.answer: Connex starts you on the pipeline with the most open deals, so you're looking at something useful right away. You can switch to another anytime.

items.question: What if we don't have any deals yet?
items.answer: You'll see a friendly starting screen with links to create your first deal or set up a pipeline. Nothing breaks, and each chart simply shows a short 'nothing to show yet' note until there's something to display.

items.question: Can I dig into the detail?
items.answer: Yes. Pipeline names, people, and deals are all links straight to their full records, and each panel has an info icon explaining what it measures.

relationship-map.title: Relationship map
relationship-map.description: An interactive graph of people, companies, and how they connect.

blocks.text: The relationship map is an interactive picture of your world: your company at the centre, your team around it, the companies you work with, and the people at those companies, with lines showing how everyone connects. Start at the centre and expand the parts you care about to explore deals, revenue, and how warm each relationship is.

blocks.name: relationship-map
blocks.caption: People and companies, and how they connect

items.title: Your company
items.description: Sits at the centre and anchors everything.

items.title: Team members
items.description: Your people, in the first ring around your company.

items.title: Client companies
items.description: The companies you work with, shown with their logos.

items.title: Contacts
items.description: The people at those companies, on the outer ring.

items.title: Expand a node
items.description: Click any company or contact to open a card with the details, like industry, revenue, recent engagement, and contact info.

items.title: Hover to trace
items.description: Hover a node to light up its whole chain, everyone above and below it, while the rest fades back.

items.title: Drag to reposition
items.description: Grab any node and move it. The map gently rearranges itself so it stays balanced.

items.title: Zoom and fit
items.description: Controls in the corner let you zoom in and out, fit everything on screen, or lock the view in place.

items.title: Legend
items.description: Open the legend in the corner for a full key to node types, connections, and deal statuses.

items.title: Warmth at a glance
items.description: Each node is tinted by how warm the relationship is, hot to cold. Contacts you've been active with get a solid green outline; quiet ones get a dashed one.

items.title: What the lines mean
items.description: Different lines show different ties: who works where, which relationships carry deals, and known connections without deals. Each deal is marked with its status: green for won, red for lost, and blue for open.

items.title: Hover a line
items.description: Hover a line that carries deals to see each deal on it, with its name and status.

blocks.title: How the map stays fresh
blocks.body: To keep things quick, most of the map loads instantly from what your browser already has, while relationship warmth is always pulled fresh so it stays accurate. Website links on the cards open safely in a new tab.

calendar.title: Calendar
calendar.description: Your meetings and events tied back to the relationships they involve.

blocks.text: The calendar gathers everything happening across your workspace, tasks, activities, deals, and notes, onto the days they belong to. You can view it by month, week, or day, or as a simple list. It's a clean way to see what's coming and what just happened, all in one place.

items.title: Tasks
items.description: In your brand colour.

items.title: Activities
items.description: In blue.

items.title: Deals
items.description: In amber.

items.title: Notes
items.description: In muted grey.

items.title: Move back and forward
items.description: Step back and forward through time with the arrows at the top.

items.title: Jump to today
items.description: The Today button brings you back to the current day, and today's date is marked with a circle.

items.title: Most important first
items.description: Within a day, deals sit at the top, then tasks, activities, and notes, so the big items are easy to spot.

items.title: See the full detail
items.description: Click any item to open a panel with its full detail, right beside the calendar.

items.title: Jump to the record
items.description: From that panel, 'Open record' takes you to the full deal, task, activity, or note behind it.

blocks.title: Packed days stay tidy
blocks.body: Every item always lands on the right day. When a day holds more than fits, it shows the first few with a '+ more' link; open the day to see everything, so even a busy week never throws off the layout.

introductions.title: Introductions
introductions.description: Request, track, and fulfill warm introductions between contacts.

blocks.text: The introductions page helps you create warm connections between people your team already knows. Connex suggests pairs worth introducing, keeps a running history of every intro your team has made, and lets you log one yourself.

items.title: Warmth badges
items.description: A tinted chip by each name shows how warm your relationship with that person is, hot to cold.

items.title: Why they're a match
items.description: Short chips explain the link, like shared connections or a shared employer, so you can judge at a glance.

items.title: Record the intro
items.description: Marks the introduction as made, connects the two people, and adds them to your history.

items.title: Or dismiss it
items.description: Clears a pairing that doesn't fit, and Connex won't suggest it again.

blocks.title: Fast and forgiving
blocks.body: Record and Dismiss update the moment you click, so the page always feels quick. If something goes wrong, the card comes right back with a note on why, and each card only takes one action, so you can't accidentally do both.

blocks.text: Your history lists every introduction your team has made, newest first. Each row shows both people, how long ago it happened, who made it, and any note. Before anyone records an intro, you'll see a friendly prompt to connect your first two contacts.

items.title: Open the form
items.description: Use 'Log an intro' for introductions you made outside Connex or before you started using this.

items.title: Pick two people
items.description: Search and choose both contacts. You can't introduce someone to themselves.

items.title: Add a note
items.description: Optionally jot down how or why you connected them.

items.title: Record it
items.description: The button turns on once two different people are chosen, and it's saved right away.

items.question: Why did a suggestion disappear before I refreshed?
items.answer: Suggestions update live, so recording or dismissing one clears it from the list straight away.

items.question: Is the page available in Japanese?
items.answer: Yes. Every card, form, label, and message is fully translated.

warm-intro-paths.title: Warm-intro paths
warm-intro-paths.description: Reverse-introduction search for the strongest path to any target.

blocks.text: Warm-intro paths flip the usual question around. Instead of asking who can reach someone, Connex looks at the people your team already knows and finds pairs you're perfectly placed to introduce, because you know both of them but they don't yet know each other. Each pair comes with a score and a short reason. You'll find them on the introductions page, and as a quick set of top opportunities on your dashboard.

blocks.name: warm-intro-path
blocks.caption: A warm path from you to the person you want to meet

items.title: Someone you really know
items.description: Only contacts your team has actually engaged with count, so every suggestion is someone you can credibly introduce.

items.title: Not already connected
items.description: Pairs who already know each other, or that you've recorded or dismissed before, are left out.

items.title: Warm on both sides
items.description: Each suggestion shows how warm you are with both people, so a strong pairing stands out from a shaky one.

items.title: A clear reason
items.description: A short chip tells you why, like shared connections or a shared employer.

items.title: Record
items.description: Confirms the intro, connects the two people, and adds it to your history. An existing stronger connection is never weakened.

items.title: Dismiss
items.description: Sets a pair aside without recording anything, and steers future suggestions toward better matches.

items.title: Log one yourself
items.description: Record an intro between any two contacts, even one that was never suggested, with an optional note.

blocks.title: A tidy, trustworthy history
blocks.body: Your intro history is built to stay clean. Introducing the same two people again just updates the existing entry instead of duplicating it, and once an intro is recorded it stays recorded. Dismissing only affects pairs you haven't introduced yet, so your history is always accurate and never rewritten.

blocks.title: Who can do this
blocks.body: Recording and dismissing intros needs the right role, so only team members with permission to update people can act. Everything stays inside your own workspace.

items.title: Introductions
items.description: The page where these suggestions live, plus your history and manual logging.

items.title: Relationship map
items.description: See the connection map these suggestions are drawn from.

reports-and-goals.title: Reports & goals
reports-and-goals.description: Build a report from your figures, schedule it, and track targets.

text: A report turns your workspace's figures into something you can hand to somebody else. Start from one of the ready-made reports and you get a finished document immediately, or build your own by choosing measures, groupings and charts.
Reports live under Overview, alongside analytics.

items.title: A stated period
items.description: The window it covers, what it is compared against, and the moment the current-state figures were read.

items.title: An executive summary
items.description: A written opening, when AI is available on your instance. Every claim in it is checked against the figures below before it is shown.

items.title: Figures and charts
items.description: One card per measure you chose, with the total and how it moved against the previous period or its target.

items.title: An appendix you can check
items.description: Every number in the report listed as a plain table, with numbered citations, so a reader can verify any claim.

items.title: Open the report and choose to schedule delivery
items.description: Pick weekly, monthly or quarterly, the hour of day, and the time zone it should follow.

items.title: Choose who receives it
items.description: Any active members of your workspace. Each recipient has to independently have permission to see everything in the report: if one of them does not, saving the schedule fails and tells you so, rather than quietly sending them less. Members who have left the workspace are dropped from the list for you.

items.title: Let it run
items.description: Before each delivery, Connex freezes a copy of the report and sends everyone a link to that frozen copy, so every recipient sees exactly the same numbers as each other and as the link.

blocks.title: Snapshots are kept, but not forever
blocks.body: Scheduled deliveries keep the most recent copies per schedule, and older ones are cleared away. A link from an old email may eventually tell you the frozen copy is no longer available and offer you the live report instead. That is expected: you get a page offering you the live report, rather than an error.

blocks.title: Saving a schedule changes whose permissions it runs with
blocks.body: A scheduled report is generated as a particular person, so it can only ever include what that person may see. Whoever saves the schedule becomes that person. If someone else edits your schedule, it will run with their access from then on.

blocks.title: Getting a report out of Connex

items.title: Snapshot
items.description: Freeze the report as it stands, so you can point at a version that will not move. Frozen copies never regenerate their written summary.

items.title: CSV
items.description: Downloads the appendix, meaning every figure as data. The written summary is not included.

items.title: Image
items.description: Exports the report as a PNG image, rendered in your browser, for pasting into a deck or a message.

items.title: Print or PDF
items.description: Opens your browser's print dialog, where you can save to PDF. There is no separate server-generated file.

blocks.text: A goal is a revenue target for one month or quarter, set for a single owner or for the whole workspace. The goals page is where you record targets; progress against them appears inside monthly and quarterly reports as an attainment figure, computed from won revenue in the same period and currency.

items.question: The summary says it is unavailable. Is the report broken?
items.answer: No. The figures and the appendix are always complete on their own. Only the written opening depends on AI, and that is switched off unless your organisation has set it up.

items.question: Who can delete a report?
items.answer: The person who created it, or a workspace administrator. Because deleting a report also destroys its frozen copies, an administrator is required when it holds copies belonging to someone else or created by a schedule.

items.question: Why does the goals page not show progress?
items.answer: It is a register of targets. Attainment is calculated inside a monthly or quarterly report, which is where you can see it against the rest of the figures.

items.title: Analytics
items.description: The live dashboards the report figures are drawn from.

items.description: What grounds the written summary, and when it refuses to write one.

DocsActivity.title: Activity
DocsActivity.description: Notes, tasks, activities, and calendar events: the signals behind warmth.
DocsActivity.lead: Activity is where the relationship signal comes from. Everything you log here feeds warmth and keeps history complete.

notes.title: Notes
notes.description: Freeform context logged against any record, with mentions.

blocks.text: Notes are where you jot down what matters. What was said on a call, what someone cares about, what to do next. Link a note to a contact or a deal and it lives right on their history, ready the moment you need it. Every linked note also helps keep that relationship warm.

items.title: Type your note
items.description: The box is ready and waiting, so just start writing. Short reminders and long recaps are equally welcome.

items.title: Link it to a contact or deal
items.description: This is what gives the note context. Linked notes are shared with everyone in your workspace.

items.title: Save
items.description: Your note is filed against the record and shows up in your notes. That's it.

blocks.title: A note with no link stays private
blocks.body: Skip the link and the note is just for you. Only you can see it, and it shows a small lock with a Private label. Want to share it with your team? Link it to a contact or deal.

blocks.title: Ways to work with your notes

items.title: Grid or table
items.description: See your notes as cards or as a sortable list, whichever you prefer. Click any note to open and edit it.

items.title: Group them
items.description: Gather your notes by the person or the company they belong to, so related ones sit together.

items.title: Search everything
items.description: Find a note by its text, the person or deal it's linked to, or who wrote it.

items.title: Edit several at once
items.description: Select a few notes and edit or delete them together, so you're not repeating yourself.

blocks.title: Turn a note into a mini-doc
blocks.body: Put a line break after your first line and it becomes a bold heading, with the rest as the body. A simple way to keep longer notes tidy.

items.question: Who can see my private notes?
items.answer: Just you. A note with no linked contact or deal is yours alone. Link it to a record whenever you want to share it with your team.

items.question: Can I change who wrote a note later?
items.answer: No. The original author stays with the note. Editing changes the text and links, not who wrote it.

tasks.title: Tasks
tasks.description: Follow-ups with due dates, assignment, and completion.

blocks.text: Tasks are your follow-ups. Give one a due date, hand it to a teammate, and link it to the contact or deal it's about. Then track it all the way to done. Changes show up for everyone right away, so whoever owns a task always sees the latest.

items.title: Say what needs doing
items.description: A short, action-focused description works best.

items.title: Give it an owner
items.description: Every task goes to someone on your team. That's who will pick it up, so choose the right person.

items.title: Add a due date and links
items.description: Optionally set when it's due and link it to a contact or deal, so it turns up in the right place.

blocks.title: Where your tasks show up
rows: Unfinished tasks past their due date.
Tasks that still need an owner.
Every unfinished task in your workspace.

items.title: Grouped for you
items.description: Tasks sort into Overdue, Today, Upcoming, and No date, so the urgent ones rise to the top.

items.title: Color-coded due dates
items.description: Red means overdue, your brand color means today, and gray means later. Finished tasks drop the date.

items.title: Today at a glance
items.description: A summary at the top of your task list shows how many of today's tasks are done, what's overdue, and how much you wrapped up this week.

items.title: See who's on it
items.description: Each task shows its owner, plus quick links to the linked contact and deal.

blocks.title: Tick it off when it's done
blocks.body: You complete a task with the round checkbox on its row. Tick it and it's marked done for everyone right away, wherever the task appears.

items.question: How do I find one task in the pile?
items.answer: Search by its description, the contact or deal it's linked to, or the owner's name. You can also filter any list by owner, contact, deal, or company.

items.question: Does anyone get told about tasks?
items.answer: Yes. Creating, updating, and completing a task keeps the people involved in the loop in real time.

items.question: How do I edit a task?
items.answer: Open it to change the description, due date, owner, or links, or to mark it done with the completed checkbox.

activities.title: Activities
activities.description: Calls, meetings, and touchpoints that record real interaction.

blocks.text: Activities are your record of what actually happened. A call, an email, a meeting, a quick note, anything worth remembering. Give each one a type, a subject, and the time it happened, then link it to a contact or deal. These are the touchpoints that keep your relationships warm.

blocks.name: activity-timeline
blocks.caption: A timeline of your recent interactions

items.title: Pick a type
items.description: Choose Call, Email, Meeting, Note, or Other. Each has its own color and icon on your timeline.

items.title: Add a subject and time
items.description: Give it a title and set when it happened. Add notes if you want to capture the detail.

items.title: Link it to a record
items.description: Attach it to a contact or deal so it lands in their history.

blocks.title: Activity types
rows: A sparkles icon, for anything that doesn't fit the rest.

blocks.text: Your activities line up newest first, grouped by day into Today, Yesterday, and so on. Each one shows its type, subject, a preview, who logged it, and the records it touches. Click a badge to jump to that record, or click the activity to edit it. A small chart up top shows your activity over the past week.

items.title: Filter by type
items.description: Show just calls, just meetings, or everything. Your choice sticks between visits.

items.title: Filter by who or what
items.description: Narrow to a person, deal, company, or the teammate who logged it.

items.title: Search
items.description: Look across subjects, notes, and the names linked to each activity.

items.title: Reset
items.description: Clear your search and filters and get back to the full timeline in one click.

calendar-events.title: Calendar events
calendar-events.description: Meetings connected to the people and companies involved.

blocks.text: Connex has a Calendar that lays your work out by date, so you can see what's coming and what just happened at a glance. It gathers the records you already keep and shows them in one place: tasks on their due date, activities like calls, emails, and meetings on the day they happened, deals on their expected close date, and your notes. There's nothing extra to maintain, it's the same records on a calendar.

blocks.title: Four ways to look at it

items.title: Month
items.description: See the whole month at a glance, with each day's items in place.

items.title: Week
items.description: Take in a single week, day by day.

items.title: Day
items.description: Zoom in on one day and everything on it.

items.title: Agenda
items.description: A simple running list of what's ahead.

blocks.title: What appears on your calendar
rows: Calls, emails, meetings, and more, on the day they happened.

blocks.title: Show only what you need
blocks.body: Use the Tasks, Activities, Deals, and Notes toggles to focus on one kind or a few. Your choice is remembered for next time, and at least one kind always stays on so the calendar is never blank.

items.title: Pick the day
items.description: Select a day on the calendar so anything you add lands on the right date.

items.title: Open the Create button
items.description: The round Create button in the bottom corner opens a short menu.

items.title: Choose what to add
items.description: Pick a new task, activity, or deal and fill in the details. The day you picked is filled in for you.

blocks.title: Open it, or move it to another day
blocks.body: Tap any item to see its details, including the linked contact or deal, and open the full record. Need it on a different day? Change the date right there, or on a computer drag a task or deal to another day on the month grid. Its record updates to match.

items.title: Activities
items.description: Log calls, emails, meetings, and other touchpoints.

items.title: Notes
items.description: Capture freeform context against a record.

items.title: Tasks
items.description: Follow-ups with due dates and assignment.

DocsLibrary.title: Library
DocsLibrary.description: Tags, files, saved views, and segments that organize your workspace.
DocsLibrary.lead: The library holds the reusable structure of your workspace: how records are labeled, filed, and sliced.

tags.title: Tags
tags.description: Flexible labels for grouping and filtering records.

blocks.text: Tags are simple labels you add to contacts, companies, deals, and files. Use them to group related records any way that makes sense to you, then filter by a tag to pull that group back up in seconds. The tag library is your home base for creating and managing every tag, each with its own color.

blocks.title: What you can do with tags

items.title: Color-code
items.description: Give each tag a color so it stands out at a glance. Pick from a set of ready-made colors, or choose your own.

items.title: Search
items.description: Find any tag by name so you can jump straight to it.

items.title: Sort
items.description: Order your tags by color or by name to keep the list tidy.

items.title: Tag in bulk
items.description: Select several records at once to add or remove a tag on all of them in one go. You can also tag files in bulk from the files library.

blocks.title: Copy a color
blocks.body: Click a tag's color code to copy it, handy when you want to match it in another tool.

blocks.title: Starting fresh
blocks.body: A brand-new workspace has no tags yet. The tag library walks you through creating your first one.

files.title: Files
files.description: Attachments stored against records, with previews and detail.

blocks.text: The Files library brings every file in your workspace together in one place. Each file is attached to a record, whether that's a company, contact, deal, or teammate, so you can browse, search, filter, tag, and manage them all from here.

items.title: Two views
items.description: Switch between a grid of thumbnails and a detailed list, whichever suits the moment.

items.title: Search
items.description: Look up any file by name across your whole workspace.

items.title: Sort
items.description: Order files by newest, oldest, name, or size.

items.title: Filter
items.description: Narrow the list by file type, by the kind of record it's attached to, or by tag. You can also surface unlinked files, whose owning record was deleted.

items.title: Detail panel
items.description: A side panel with the file's type, size, who uploaded it and when, the record it belongs to, and its tags.

items.title: Related files
items.description: See everything else attached to the same record and jump between them.

items.title: Linked record
items.description: Open the company, person, deal, or teammate the file belongs to in one click.

items.title: Image preview
items.description: Pictures show a thumbnail on the card and a full-size preview in the detail panel.

items.title: Open or download
items.description: Open a file in a new tab or save it to your device straight from the library.

items.title: Tags at a glance
items.description: Tags show as colored chips on every file, with extra ones tucked into a tidy count.

items.title: Bulk actions
items.description: Select several files to tag or delete them together.

items.title: Delete safely
items.description: Removing a file asks you to confirm first, so nothing goes by accident.

blocks.title: Share the exact view
blocks.body: Send a teammate a link and it opens right where you left off, filters and all, even down to a specific file.

blocks.title: Nothing here yet
blocks.body: When your workspace has no files, you'll see a friendly prompt pointing you to a record where you can open it and attach your first file.

saved-views-and-segments.title: Saved views & segments
saved-views-and-segments.description: Reusable, rule-based slices of your records you can return to.

blocks.text: Saved views let you keep a filtered, searched, and sorted list of records so you never have to rebuild it. They work across companies, contacts, and deals, and each view is yours alone. Smart segments take it further, letting you save a set of rules that pulls the right records automatically.

items.title: Save a view
items.description: Capture your current filters, search, sort order, and any segments as a named view you can return to.

items.title: Update
items.description: Tweak a view and save your changes over it.

items.title: Save as new
items.description: Keep the original as-is and save your changes under a new name.

items.title: Rename or delete
items.description: Give a view a clearer name, or remove one you no longer need.

items.title: Quick tabs
items.description: Your views appear as tabs at the top. The 'All' tab is the full, unfiltered list.

blocks.title: Your tabs stay in sync
blocks.body: Adjust your filters by hand until they match a saved view, and that view's tab lights up on its own. The tabs always reflect what you're currently looking at.

blocks.text: A smart segment is a set of rules that finds matching records for you. You can mix everyday details like industry or tag with Connex's relationship signals, and decide whether records must match every rule or just one of them.

blocks.title: Segment examples (companies)
rows: Companies where someone you know well can introduce you.
Companies with at least one deal still in progress.
Companies where things are going quiet.
Companies you haven't emailed, called, met, or noted in a while. You choose the time window.

items.title: Field rules
items.description: Match by industry, by part of a name, or by a tag.

items.title: Match all or any
items.description: Require every rule to match, or just one of them.

items.title: Flip a rule
items.description: Invert any rule, like 'does not have an open deal' or 'is not in Fintech'.

items.title: Ready-made choices
items.description: Dropdowns fill in with your workspace's industries and tags, so you're not typing from scratch.

items.title: Clear as you go
items.description: See each rule as a chip, and clear them all to start over.

blocks.title: Only what you're allowed to see
blocks.body: A segment always respects your roles and permissions, so it returns just the records you have access to in your workspace.

items.question: Are my saved views shared with my team?
items.answer: No. Your saved views are yours alone. Teammates keep their own and can't see yours.

items.question: Can a saved view include a segment?
items.answer: Yes. A view remembers your filters, search, sort, and any smart segment, so opening it brings the segment back too.

documents-and-approvals.title: Documents & approvals
documents-and-approvals.description: Build a template once, generate quotes from deals, and require sign-off before finalising.

text: A document template is a reusable layout for something you send to a customer, like a quote. You build it once with headings, lists and merge fields, and then generate a document from any deal.
Templates live in the library. Documents themselves live on the deal they were generated from.

blocks.name: document-approval
blocks.caption: A document waiting for approval, and the rule that the person who wrote it is not the person who approves it.

items.title: Blocks, not a word processor
items.description: Headings, paragraphs, lists, quotes and dividers, added from a toolbar or by typing a slash.

items.title: A line items block
items.description: Drops in the deal's line items and totals wherever you put it, so a quote is always the deal's real numbers.

items.title: Merge fields
items.description: Small chips for the company name and address, the deal name and currency, the owner, the workspace, today's date and the total.

items.title: Managed by permission
items.description: Creating and editing templates is a separate permission from generating documents, so you can let a team use templates without changing them.

blocks.title: A generated document never changes again
blocks.body: Generating freezes everything: the resolved wording, the deal's line items and its totals as they were at that moment. There is no way to edit a document afterwards, by design. To correct one, generate a new version and mark the old one superseded. Later edits to the template or to the deal's line items never reach back into it.

blocks.title: What each status means
rows: Newly generated. This is the only status that can be deleted.
Sent for sign-off and waiting on a decision.
Signed off, and ready to be finalised.
The version you stand behind. The draft watermark disappears from the printed copy.
Replaced by a newer version. Nothing comes back out of this state.

blocks.text: An approval policy describes when sign-off is required, for example above a certain total in a given currency, or beyond a certain discount. Policies are matched against the document's frozen figures, and the first active policy that matches is the one that applies.

items.title: You cannot finalise around it
items.description: If an active policy matches a draft, finalising is refused until the document has been approved. The approved and pending states can only ever be set by the approval process itself, never requested directly.

items.title: You cannot approve your own work
items.description: A decision is refused if you wrote the document or if you were the one who sent it for approval. Someone else with permission to approve has to decide.

items.title: One decision settles it
items.description: There is a single approver rather than a chain or a quorum. Approving moves the document on; rejecting returns it to draft so it can be reworked.

items.title: The requester can withdraw
items.description: Whoever asked for approval can cancel the request and return the document to draft.

blocks.title: The approve action is offered more widely than it is allowed
blocks.body: If you generated a document that a colleague then sent for approval, the approve and reject actions still appear to you. Choosing one is refused with a message explaining why. The rule is enforced properly; it is only the menu that has not caught up.

items.question: How do I get a PDF?
items.answer: Use the PDF action, which opens a clean print view and your browser's print dialog. From there, save as PDF.

items.question: Who can delete a document?
items.answer: Only drafts can be deleted at all, and only by the person who generated them or by a workspace administrator.

items.question: We turned off a policy. Can old drafts now be finalised?
items.answer: Drafts, yes. The requirement is checked at the moment you finalise, against the policies that are active then, so deactivating a policy releases anything still in draft. A document already sent for approval stays where it is, because that decision has to be made or withdrawn before it can move on.

items.title: Products and line items
items.description: The line items and totals a document freezes.

items.title: Members and roles
items.description: Who holds the permission to approve.

DocsData.title: Search, import & data
DocsData.description: Global search, filters, bulk operations, import/export, and custom fields.
DocsData.lead: These tools move data in and out of Connex and help you find and change it at scale.

search.title: Global search
search.description: Search across every record type with keyboard navigation.

blocks.text: One search bar finds everything in your workspace. Start typing and Connex looks through your people, companies, deals, pipelines, tags, notes, tasks, activities, and files all at once. Two letters is enough to get going, and results update as you type.

blocks.name: global-search
blocks.caption: Search across everything in your workspace

items.title: Everything in one place
items.description: A single search covers people, companies, deals, pipelines, tags, notes, tasks, activities, and attachments.

items.title: Tidy, grouped results
items.description: Matches are sorted into groups by type, so people stay with people and deals stay with deals.

items.title: Enough to spot a match
items.description: Each result shows an avatar or icon, a name, and a helpful detail like an email, job title, industry, or deal value.

items.title: Quick look or full page
items.description: See a few results in the dropdown, or open the full search page to browse every match with a count for each group.

items.action: Move up and down through the results
Open the highlighted result, or the full search page if none is highlighted

blocks.title: Not finding it?
blocks.body: Search needs at least two letters to start, so a single letter won't pull up results yet. If a name looks cut off, open the result to see the whole thing.

filters-and-bulk.title: Filters & bulk actions
filters-and-bulk.description: Narrow a table, select many rows, and act on them at once.

blocks.text: Your contact, company, and deal lists all share the same toolbar: filters to narrow the list down, and bulk actions to change many records at once. Use them together. Filter to exactly the records you want, then update all of them in one go.

items.title: Pick several values
items.description: Choose more than one company, job title, or tag at a time to match any of several values.

items.title: Single-choice controls
items.description: Set things like the sort order or how the list is displayed.

items.title: Contact-specific filters
items.description: The contacts list adds company and job-title filters, plus a 'No company' option to find people who aren't linked to one yet.

items.title: See what's active
items.description: Applied filters appear as removable pills, and each active filter turns colored with a count of how many values you've picked, so you can tell at a glance what's narrowing your list. Clear one at a time, or reset them all.

items.title: Add or remove tags
items.description: Tick the records you want, then add or remove a tag across all of them at once.

items.title: Delete in bulk
items.description: Remove every selected record in one step.

items.title: Reassign deal owners
items.description: Hand selected deals to a new owner, or clear the owner. The new owner needs to be a member of your workspace.

items.title: Move deal stages
items.description: Push selected deals to a different stage in your pipeline.

blocks.title: One problem won't stop the rest
blocks.body: Bulk actions handle each record on its own. If one can't be updated, the others still go through, and you get a clear count of what succeeded and what didn't, with the reason for anything that failed. Even very large selections are handled smoothly.

import-and-export.title: Import & export
import-and-export.description: Bring records in from CSV and take your data back out.

blocks.text: Importing brings records into Connex from a spreadsheet (CSV) file, and exporting takes your data back out as a clean file you can open in Excel or Google Sheets. The import runs as a friendly step-by-step wizard, and you always see a preview of exactly what will happen before anything is created or changed.

blocks.name: import-wizard
blocks.caption: Matching spreadsheet columns to Connex fields

items.title: Upload
items.description: Choose your CSV file. Connex checks it right away and shows you what it found.

items.title: Match columns
items.description: Line up each column in your file with a field in Connex. You can also create a new field on the spot, or skip a column you don't need.

items.title: Preview
items.description: See exactly what will happen for every row, including any matches to records you already have and any errors. Nothing is saved yet.

items.title: Finish
items.description: Confirm, and Connex creates and updates your records. You'll see how many were created, updated, and skipped.

items.title: Tags come along
items.description: A column named 'tags' can list several tags separated by commas or semicolons. Any that don't exist yet are created for you.

items.title: Companies link automatically
