items.description: When you import contacts with a company column, Connex links each person to their company, creates the company if it's new, and records their work history.

items.title: People link to deals
items.description: Import deals with a list of contact emails and Connex connects the matching people for you. Emails it doesn't recognise are simply skipped.

items.title: Pipelines and stages by name
items.description: Just name the pipeline and stage for each deal. If you leave them out, the deal lands in your first pipeline and stage.

blocks.title: Duplicates are handled for you
blocks.body: Connex spots when a row matches a record you already have, based on things like a contact's email or a company's website. You choose what happens: fill in only the blanks, skip the row, or overwrite with the new details. And if the same record appears twice in your file, it's only added once. You can also link a row to a specific record by hand during the preview.

blocks.title: Fix any errors and try again
body: If some rows can't be imported, the last step gives you a 'Download errors' file. It's just those rows plus a note explaining what went wrong, so you can fix them and import again.
One thing to keep in mind: files need to stay under 5 MB and 5,000 rows.

blocks.text: Taking your data out

items.title: Respects your filters
items.description: Export matches whatever you're looking at. Filter your list first, and only those records come out.

items.title: Includes your custom fields
items.description: Your export has the standard columns, a column for each of your custom fields, and a tags column.

items.title: Ready for your spreadsheet
items.description: Files open cleanly in Excel and Google Sheets, with accented and non-English characters shown correctly.

items.title: Safe to open
items.description: Connex protects your export against sneaky spreadsheet formulas, so files are safe to open and share.

custom-fields.title: Custom fields
custom-fields.description: Extend records with fields specific to your workspace.

blocks.text: Custom fields let you track things Connex doesn't include by default, like a customer number, a renewal date, or a yes/no flag. Each one belongs to a type of record, holds a specific kind of value, and shows up right on your record pages and in your exports next to the built-in fields.

The easiest way to add a custom field is right from the import wizard. When one of your columns doesn't match an existing field, choose 'Create custom field' while matching columns, pick a type, and Connex creates it for you the first time you import. It even suggests a likely type based on your data.

blocks.title: What makes up a custom field

items.title: Which records it's for
items.description: Each field belongs to one kind of record, so a field on contacts is separate from one on companies or deals.

items.title: A name you choose
items.description: The label you type is the name you'll see on records and in exports.

items.title: A value type
items.description: Pick text, number, date, yes/no, or web address. The type decides what values are allowed and how they show up.

items.title: Where it shows up
items.description: Once created, it appears on matching record pages and as its own column in exports.

blocks.title: What each type accepts
rows: true or false, yes or no, or 1 or 0.
A full link or a plain domain.

blocks.title: Create it once, use it everywhere
blocks.body: A custom field you make during import sticks around as a reusable field, not a one-time value. From then on it shows on every matching record and gets its own column in future exports.

items.title: Import & export
items.description: Match columns, create fields on the fly, and see how custom fields flow into your exported files.

DocsCollaboration.title: Collaboration
DocsCollaboration.description: Invites, invite links, record sharing, permissions, notifications, and mentions.
DocsCollaboration.lead: Connex works best with your whole team. These pages cover how you bring people in and work together, while keeping each workspace private.

invites-and-links.title: Invites & invite links
invites-and-links.description: Add teammates directly or with a shareable link.

text: Connex is better with your team, and adding people takes just a moment. If you are an admin or owner, you can invite someone by email or share a link that lets a group join. Either way, the new person confirms before they get access, and they join with the role you choose.

items.title: Invite by email
items.description: Enter someone's email address and choose a role. Connex creates an invitation, and they show up as pending until they accept. If they do not have a Connex account yet, they get a link to sign up and join.

items.title: Add an existing user
items.description: Already on Connex? When you invite their email address, they are added right away as pending and get a heads-up in their notifications. They join once they accept.

items.title: Share a link
items.description: Create a link and send it to a whole group. Anyone who opens it can join with the role you chose, until it expires or you turn it off.

items.title: One invite at a time
items.description: Each email can have one open invite. Sending a new one simply replaces the old one.

items.title: Open the invitation
items.description: Find it under Pending invitations in your settings, or click the link you were sent. Either one opens a preview.

items.title: Check the details
items.description: You will see the workspace name, the role you are being given, and who invited you. If a link is expired or already used up, you get a clear message instead.

items.title: Accept or decline
items.description: Accept to join with your role, or decline to remove the invitation. It is entirely up to you.

blocks.title: An invite goes to one address
blocks.body: An email invite is meant for the exact address it was sent to. If you are signed in with a different email, Connex lets you know the invite went elsewhere. Sign in with the right account and you are in.

blocks.title: Link settings
rows: Choose whether people join as a member or an admin. This is set when you create the link.
How long the link stays active, in days. Leave it empty to use the default.
Cap how many people can join through it. Leave it empty for no limit.
Set separately as a workspace-wide list, allowed domains limit invite links to people whose email matches one of them. Leave the list empty to let anyone in.

items.question: Where do I see what is outstanding?
items.answer: Go to Settings then Members. You will find Pending Invites (email invites not yet accepted) and Active Links (links still working), each showing its role and expiry. Links also show how many people have joined.

items.question: How do I share an invite or link?
items.answer: Copy the accept link from any pending invite, or use the copy button next to an active link. A quick checkmark confirms it copied.

items.question: Can I cancel an invite?
items.answer: Yes. Revoke a pending invite and it is gone, so it can no longer be accepted.

items.question: How do I turn off a shareable link?
items.answer: Revoke it. The link drops off your list and stops letting anyone else join.

sharing-and-permissions.title: Sharing & permissions
sharing-and-permissions.description: Share individual records and control who can see what.

text: Two things control who can see and do what. Roles set what each person can do inside your workspace. Sharing lets you show a single record to another workspace you also belong to.
Admins and owners manage roles and membership, and every change is recorded.

items.title: Owner
items.description: Full control. Owners manage people, roles, and sharing, can hand ownership to someone else, and can delete the workspace.

items.title: Admin
items.description: Manages people, invites, and sharing. Admins can do almost everything except delete the workspace.

items.title: Member
items.description: Works with records day to day, without the admin controls.

blocks.text: Need something in between? Owners can build custom roles. Pick exactly which actions a role can take, such as creating or editing companies, then assign it to people in place of a built-in role. You can edit or delete a custom role later, and Connex makes sure no one is left on a role that no longer exists by moving them first.

items.title: See everyone
items.description: Every member appears with their name, email, role, and photo. Your own row is marked You, and anyone who has not accepted yet shows a Pending badge.

items.title: Change roles
items.description: Promote or demote between member and admin, assign a custom role, or hand ownership to someone else.

items.title: Remove members
items.description: Remove anyone but yourself, and it takes effect right away. A workspace always needs one owner, so pass ownership on before you step down.

blocks.text: Sometimes a company, contact, or pipeline needs to be visible to another team you work with. You can share one your workspace owns with another workspace you belong to. Your workspace stays the owner, and the other workspace gets to view it.

blocks.title: Sharing rules
rows: Shared records are view-only for the other workspace.
You can share with the other workspaces you are a member of. You cannot share somewhere you do not belong.
A record cannot be shared back with its own workspace.
See every workspace a record is shared with, and unshare any of them whenever you like. It disappears from the other team right away.

blocks.title: Everything is recorded
blocks.body: Invites, links, shares, and member changes are all recorded, so there is a clear account of who did what and when.

notifications-and-mentions.title: Notifications & mentions
notifications-and-mentions.description: Stay in the loop with an inbox and @-mentions on records.

text: Connex keeps an eye on your data and raises notifications so you do not have to remember everything. Tasks that are due, deals that are closing, relationships that are cooling, and people worth introducing all surface on their own.
Everything from every workspace you belong to lands in one inbox, so switching workspaces never changes what you see. When a teammate mentions you on a record, that shows up here too.

blocks.name: notification-inbox
blocks.caption: Your notification inbox

items.title: Task reminders
items.description: A heads-up when a task is due soon, and again once it is overdue. You can tick the task complete straight from the notification.

items.title: Deal close-date reminders
items.description: A nudge as a deal's expected close date approaches, and a stronger one once it passes. The deal owner and everyone on the deal team get it.

items.title: Relationship cooling nudges
items.description: A gentle reminder when you have not been in touch with someone for a while. Each one offers a Log a touch button to warm things back up.

items.title: Introduction opportunities
items.description: A suggestion when two people in your network are worth introducing to each other, shared with your team.

blocks.title: Why a nudge is marked Priority
rows: A related deal is expected to close very soon.
The deal is one of your larger ones by value.
The deal is near the end of its pipeline.
This person plays a decision-making role, like a champion or buyer.

blocks.text: The bell at the top of the sidebar shows how many unread notifications you have, and it keeps itself up to date. Click it for a quick peek at your latest unread items, or open the full inbox to see everything with clear timestamps and an icon for each type. Notifications from your other workspaces carry a small tag so you always know where they came from.

blocks.title: What you can do with a notification

items.title: Read and unread
items.description: Mark anything read or unread, or clear the list with Mark all read.

items.title: Dismiss and restore
items.description: Dismiss something to tuck it into History, and bring it back if you need it again.

items.title: Snooze
items.description: Hide a notification for a day, a few days, or a week. It returns if the situation still needs you.

items.title: Act right away
items.description: Tick a task complete right from the notification, open a cooling relationship to reach out, or jump to the record behind any alert. The same alerts also appear on the matching contact, deal, or task.

blocks.title: Inbox views
rows: Your current notifications, read and unread.
Things you dismissed, plus ones Connex resolved on its own.

blocks.title: Nudges will not nag you
body: Once a cooling nudge appears it stays until the relationship truly warms up or you reach out, so a small dip in the trend will not make it flicker back at you.
Opening a notification's record also marks it read, so acting on something quietly clears it for you.

items.question: Can I turn off types I do not want?
items.answer: Yes. In notification settings you can switch task reminders, deal reminders, and relationship cooling nudges on or off on their own, so you only hear about what matters to you.

items.question: Why did my old overdue items not appear?
items.answer: When you first start, Connex will not flood you with ancient history. It only brings in recently overdue tasks and deals, and skips relationships that have been cold for a long time. New nudges still appear as normal.

items.question: Are due dates in my time zone?
items.answer: Yes. Reminders use your local time zone, so a task due on the 24th is judged by your date, not somewhere else's.

items.question: What happens when someone mentions me?
items.answer: When a teammate mentions you on a record, you get a notification right here alongside the rest. The person you mention needs to be a member of the workspace.

DocsSettings.title: Settings & administration
DocsSettings.description: Members, roles and permissions, rules and automation, notification settings, and audit logs.
DocsSettings.lead: Administration controls who can do what, automates routine work, and keeps a record of every change.

members-and-roles.title: Members & roles
members-and-roles.description: Manage who is in the workspace and what their role permits.

text: Your workspace is your team's private space, and only the people you add can see it. What each person can do depends on their role. This is where you invite teammates, set their roles, and decide who can manage what.

Anyone with the admin role or higher can add and manage people. Owners sit at the top and can hand full control to someone else. You'll find all of this in your workspace settings, right next to rules, custom fields, and notifications.

blocks.title: The roles you can give people

items.title: Owner
items.description: Full control over everything, including creating custom roles. Every workspace needs at least one owner.

items.title: Admin
items.description: Manages people, invites, custom fields, and most settings. Can do almost everything an owner can.

items.title: Member
items.description: The everyday role. Works with your records based on the permissions you've granted.

items.title: Custom roles
items.description: Owners can build their own roles and choose exactly which actions each one allows. Great for fitting Connex to how your team works.

items.title: Invite by email
items.description: Enter someone's email and they get an invitation. If they already use Connex, they'll see it right away in the app. Otherwise they get an invite link that's good for a limited time.

items.title: Share an invite link
items.description: Create a reusable link you can send to several people at once. Set how long it lasts or a limit on uses, and revoke it anytime.

items.title: Auto-join by email domain
items.description: Add your company's email domain and anyone who signs up with a matching address joins automatically as a member. Handy for onboarding a whole team.

items.title: Accept, decline, or leave
items.description: Invitees can accept or decline from their Membership tab, and leave a workspace whenever they like.

items.question: Can I change or remove myself?
items.answer: No. Your own row is locked so you can't accidentally change your role or remove yourself. Ask another owner or admin if you need a change.

items.question: What if I don't have permission for a section?
items.answer: You'll see a friendly no-access message instead. Just ask an owner or admin to make the change, or to adjust your role.

items.question: Why did my change snap back?
items.answer: Your changes show instantly, then save in the background. If something goes wrong, the change reverts and you'll see a quick error message. Give it another try in a moment.

rules-and-automation.title: Rules & automation
rules-and-automation.description: Automate routine changes with workspace rules.

text: Rules take care of the repetitive stuff for you. Set one up once, and whenever something happens, like a deal is won or a company goes quiet, Connex runs the steps you chose automatically. No reminders to yourself, no manual busywork.
Anyone with permission to manage rules can create them, and you can switch any rule on or off whenever you like.

items.title: The trigger
items.description: What sets the rule off. Usually a change to a record, like a deal moving to a new stage. It can also run on a schedule.

items.title: A condition (optional)
items.description: A way to narrow things down so the rule only runs for the records you care about. Available for company rules.

items.title: The actions
items.description: What Connex does when the rule runs. You can line up several steps.

items.title: Who it runs as
items.description: A rule can act as you, using your permissions, or as the workspace itself for team-wide automation.

blocks.title: What can set off a rule
rows: Created, moved to a new stage, won, lost, or updated.
Created or updated. Companies can also run on a schedule.

blocks.title: What a rule can do
rows: Sends someone an in-app notification with your message.
Adds a task with a title and a due date, three days out by default.
Records an activity, like a note or a call.
Applies a tag you've already set up.

blocks.title: Schedules keep an eye on your companies
blocks.body: Besides reacting to changes, a rule can run on a repeating schedule, hourly, daily, or weekly, for your companies. Pair it with a condition (say, companies that have gone quiet or have an open deal) and Connex checks in for you on its own. It won't run twice for the same window, so you won't get duplicates.

items.question: Can I turn a rule off without deleting it?
items.answer: Yes. Each rule has a switch. A paused rule keeps all its settings but won't run until you turn it back on.

items.question: Can one rule react to more than one event?
items.answer: Yes. Pick any mix of events you like. Leave it blank and the rule reacts to every change.

items.question: Can I tell what a rule does at a glance?
items.answer: Yes. Each rule shows a plain-language summary of its trigger and actions, with a badge when it's paused or set to run as the workspace.

notification-settings.title: Notification settings
notification-settings.description: Tune which events reach you and how.

text: Notifications bring what needs your attention to you, so you're not digging around to find it. A task coming due, a deal that just closed, a relationship that's starting to cool, they all land in one place, each with a link to the record behind it.
Connex keeps a running count of what's unread and updates the moment something new arrives.

items.title: See what's unread
items.description: Connex keeps a running count of what you haven't read yet and keeps it up to date.

items.title: Filter and browse
items.description: Sort through your notifications to find the ones you need.

items.title: Jump to the source
items.description: Click any notification to go straight to the deal, company, person, or task behind it.

items.title: Mark all as read
items.description: Clear your unread count all at once when you're caught up.

items.title: Mark read or unread
items.description: Keep track of what you've dealt with and what still needs a look.

items.title: Dismiss
items.description: Move a notification out of your active list once you're done with it.

items.title: Restore
items.description: Changed your mind? Bring a dismissed notification back.

items.title: Snooze
items.description: Hide a notification for now and have it come back later.

blocks.title: Snooze buys you time
blocks.body: Snoozing tucks a notification away for a while, then brings it back to your inbox. It's a way to say not now, remind me later, rather than making it disappear.

blocks.title: What Connex can notify you about
rows: A task you own is due today or already overdue.
A deal is won or lost.
A company or person you're connected to is starting to cool off.
Someone mentions you in a note, task, activity, introduction, or deal.

blocks.title: You're in control of what reaches you
blocks.body: Each kind of notification can reach you in the app, by email, or both. In-app alerts are on by default and email is off, so you'll see updates in Connex right away and can add email whenever you like.

connected-capture.title: Connected account capture
connected-capture.description: Control which provider interactions become relationship evidence.

text: Connecting Google or Microsoft gives Connex custody of a read-only provider connection. It does not start capture. Open Account, then Connections, and save a capture policy for each provider you want to use.
Policies are scoped to the active workspace. Your policy can be narrowed by workspace and operator controls, but those controls can never be widened from the account page.

items.title: Sources and history
items.description: Choose calendar, received mail, sent mail, and a history window up to 180 days. New policies start at 90 days.

items.title: Metadata and bodies
items.description: Metadata-only capture is the default. Message bodies require both workspace permission and your explicit choice.

items.title: Participant review
items.description: Unmatched or ambiguous participants stay in a review queue. Attach, create through duplicate preflight, or ignore them.

items.title: Approval and evidence
items.description: Review-first policies hold resolved items for approval. Captured activities show provider provenance and remain read-only.

blocks.title: Purge and disconnect have different scopes
blocks.body: Purge removes captured content and derived evidence from the active workspace. Disconnect purges this provider's captured data from every workspace before deleting the credential. Metadata-only audit records remain.

audit-logs.title: Audit logs
audit-logs.description: A tamper-evident history of actions taken in the workspace.

text: The audit log is a complete, unchangeable history of everything that happens in your workspace. You'll find it under Admin, then Logs, laid out as a timeline with the newest events first.

Connex records events on its own as people work, so nothing depends on anyone remembering to write it down. Once an event is recorded, it can never be edited or deleted, which makes the log a record you can trust when you need to look back.

blocks.title: Admins and owners only
blocks.body: The audit log is meant for people managing the workspace, so only admins and owners can open it. If you need to see it and can't, ask an owner to adjust your role.

items.title: Who
items.description: The person who did it, with their name saved as it was at the time, so history stays accurate even if they're renamed later. Automated actions show up as System.

items.title: What
items.description: The action they took, shown in plain language like created, updated, added tag, or logged in.

items.title: On what
items.description: The record it happened to, kept even if that record is later renamed or removed.

items.title: Outcome
items.description: Whether it succeeded or failed, so problems are easy to spot.

items.title: Search
items.description: Look up events by who did them, what they touched, or the action taken.

items.title: Filter
items.description: Narrow the list by action, record type, outcome, date range, or who did it.

items.title: See what matches
items.description: Each filter shows how many events it will find, so there are no surprises.

items.title: Sort
items.description: Flip between newest first and oldest first whenever it helps.

blocks.title: Open an event for the full story

items.title: What changed
items.description: See each field that changed, with the old value and the new one side by side.

items.title: What went wrong
items.description: If an action failed, the reason shows right at the top.

items.title: The finer details
items.description: The expanded entry also shows technical context, like the address and device the action came from.

blocks.title: Reading the log at a glance

items.question: How is everything organized?
items.answer: Events are grouped by day, with today and yesterday called out and a count for each day, so you can scan a period quickly.

items.question: How do I spot problems fast?
items.answer: Events are color-coded by type, and anything that failed carries a clear Failed badge. Filter by outcome to see just the failures.

items.question: Why do the times keep changing?
items.answer: Times show as a few minutes ago and refresh on their own. Hover over any one to see the exact date and time.

sign-in-and-security.title: Signing in & security
sign-in-and-security.description: Passwords, passkeys, single sign-on, and why sensitive actions ask you again.

text: You can sign in to Connex with a password, with a passkey, or through your organisation's identity provider if your administrator has set one up. Passkeys are always available; the rest depend on configuration.
Whichever way you sign in, your session is a cookie in your browser. Signing out ends it, and it also expires on its own after a period of inactivity and again after a longer fixed period.

items.title: Password
items.description: With your username or your email address. Always available.

items.title: Passkey
items.description: Your device's fingerprint, face or PIN, or a security key. Always available, and worth setting up even if you mainly use a password.

items.title: Google or Microsoft
items.description: Off unless your administrator has enabled it and supplied credentials for your instance.

items.title: Enterprise single sign-on
items.description: OpenID Connect or SAML, configured per organisation. Off by default.

blocks.title: Administering Connex requires a passkey
blocks.body: Sensitive actions ask you to confirm it is really you before they proceed, and that confirmation is satisfied only by a passkey. Signing in with a password does not count, no matter how recently you did it. If you administer a workspace, register a passkey before you need one, or these actions will refuse and tell you recent authentication is required.

items.title: People and access
items.description: Inviting someone, revoking an invitation, creating invite links, changing roles and permissions, and managing organisation members and allowed domains.

items.title: Connections and credentials
items.description: Setting up single sign-on, workspace email, delivery providers, your organisation's AI provider, and connecting or disconnecting your own accounts.

items.title: Your own security
items.description: Renaming or removing a passkey. Adding your first passkey is authorised by your password instead, and changing your email address is also a password check rather than a passkey one.

items.title: Data you cannot undo
items.description: Exporting a whole workspace, tearing one down, and acting on a privacy request.

items.title: You usually join rather than create
items.description: Creating a workspace is normally switched off, so new people join an existing one through an invitation or an invite link. If you sign up and land with no workspace, that is why, and an invitation is what you need.

items.title: Three built-in roles
items.description: Members do everyday CRM work. Administrators additionally manage settings, the product catalogue, goals and approvals. Owners can do everything within the workspace. Custom roles can be built from individual permissions. Exporting or removing a whole workspace is a separate, organisation-level role rather than a workspace one.

items.question: I registered a passkey. Do I still need my password?
items.answer: Keep it. A passkey is tied to the device or key you created it on, so a password remains your way in from somewhere else.

items.question: Why was I asked to confirm again straight after signing in?
items.answer: Because the confirmation is specifically a passkey check, and a password sign-in does not provide one. Register a passkey and the prompt becomes a quick tap.

items.question: Can I belong to more than one workspace?
items.answer: Yes, and you switch between them from the top of the sidebar without signing out. Records do not appear across workspaces on their own, though someone can deliberately share a company, contact or pipeline with another workspace in the same organisation.

items.title: Members and roles
items.description: Inviting people and deciding what they can do.

items.title: Workspaces and teams
items.description: What a workspace is, and why nothing crosses between them.

connected-accounts.title: Connected accounts
connected-accounts.description: Linking your Google or Microsoft account, and what that does and does not start.

text: You can connect your own Google or Microsoft account to Connex from your account settings. The connection is yours alone: nobody else in your workspace can see it or manage it, and administrators cannot connect an account on your behalf.
Connex asks only for read access to your mail and calendar. It never asks for permission to send anything as you.

blocks.title: Connecting on its own does nothing
blocks.body: Linking an account does not start reading anything. Connex only begins looking at your mail or calendar after you have chosen which sources to allow and saved that choice, and only if capture is switched on for your deployment at all. Nothing is selected for you.

items.title: Confirm it is you
items.description: Connecting is one of the actions that asks for a passkey first, because it grants Connex ongoing access to your mailbox.

items.title: Approve at the provider
items.description: You are sent to Google or Microsoft to approve. Approve everything asked for: if ongoing access is not granted, Connex refuses the connection rather than storing one that will stop working.

items.title: Decide what may be looked at
items.description: Choose the sources you want considered, within any ceiling your workspace administrator has set. If you skip this, nothing happens.

items.title: Your administrator sets the outer limit
items.description: A workspace administrator can cap what anybody may allow, for example excluding message bodies. Your own choice can be narrower than that ceiling but never wider.

items.title: Pausing keeps the connection
items.description: Pausing stops the reading without discarding the connection, and does not ask you to reconnect afterwards.

items.title: Disconnecting clears up first
items.description: Disconnecting removes everything captured through that provider from every workspace before the stored credential is destroyed. It cannot be undone, and you are asked to confirm you understand that.

items.title: Revoke Microsoft access yourself
items.description: When you disconnect Google, Connex also tells Google to revoke access. There is no equivalent for Microsoft, so remove Connex from your Microsoft account settings as well if you want access withdrawn at the provider.

blocks.title: Capture is an internal preview
blocks.body: Reading mail and calendar to capture relationship signals is not yet generally available. It stays behind provider verification that is still in progress, so on most deployments the option to connect exists while capture itself is unavailable.

items.title: Connected account capture
items.description: What is captured, how it is reviewed, and how to purge it.

items.title: Signing in and security
items.description: Why connecting asks you to confirm with a passkey.

privacy-and-data-requests.title: Privacy & data requests
privacy-and-data-requests.description: Handling a request from someone whose data you hold, and restricting processing for a contact.

text: People whose details you hold can ask you what you have, ask you to correct it, ask you to stop using it, or ask you to delete it. Connex gives organisation administrators a place to record those requests and to act on them.
This page describes the tools. It is not legal advice, and your obligations depend on your own circumstances.

items.title: A record of every request
items.description: Requests are logged at organisation level with who made them and what was asked, so you can show how and when each one was handled.

items.title: A disclosure you can hand over
items.description: Connex assembles what it holds about a person into a single disclosure, so answering an access request is not a manual search across screens.

items.title: Restrictions on a contact
items.description: Suspending processing stops scoring, automation, suggestions, AI features and exports for that contact. Ceasing third-party provision blocks new sharing and excludes them from AI entirely.

items.title: An audit trail you cannot rewrite
items.description: Actions are recorded in an append-only log with integrity protection, which is what lets you demonstrate afterwards that you did what you say you did.

blocks.title: Restricting a contact clears what AI already wrote
blocks.body: When you suspend processing or cease third-party provision for a contact, anything AI previously generated that involved them is purged, and future AI features exclude them. This happens as part of applying the restriction rather than as a separate cleanup you have to remember.

items.title: Privacy notice
items.description: The public statement of how personal data is handled.

items.title: Handling disclosure
items.description: The published detail required alongside it, covering how requests are received and handled.

items.title: Legal notices
items.description: Terms and the accompanying legal pages.

items.title: Commercial disclosure
items.description: The commercial transaction disclosure expected of a Japanese business.

blocks.title: Finish outstanding requests before removing a workspace
blocks.body: Tearing down a workspace or an organisation is refused while a data subject request is still open against it. That is deliberate: it stops a request being made unanswerable by deleting the evidence. Close out the request first, then tear down.

items.question: Who can see and act on these requests?
items.answer: Organisation administrators. Acting on one asks you to confirm with a passkey first, because the actions are not reversible.

items.question: Does restricting a contact delete them?
items.answer: No. They stay in your CRM, but Connex stops scoring, suggesting, automating and exporting them. Deletion is a separate decision.

items.question: Can I get everything in a workspace out at once?
items.answer: Yes. An organisation administrator can export an entire workspace, which is the tool for a migration or a full handover rather than for one person's request.

items.title: Audit logs
items.description: The record of what was done, by whom, and when.

items.title: Operational boundaries
items.description: Who can reach your data, and how support works without that access.

DocsPreferences.title: Preferences & the little things
DocsPreferences.description: Theming, language, keyboard shortcuts, and the small quirks worth knowing.
DocsPreferences.lead: The details. How Connex looks, speaks your language, responds to the keyboard, and the tiny behaviors that make it feel considered.

theming-and-appearance.title: Theming & appearance
theming-and-appearance.description: Light, dark, and system themes across the whole app.

text: Connex comes with a light theme, a dark theme, and a system option that follows your computer's setting. Whatever you pick applies across the whole app, from your records and charts to menus and pop-ups, and it takes effect right away with no reload.
Everything is styled to match, so colors, badges, and charts all shift together when you change themes and stay easy to read either way.

items.title: Open the theme menu
items.description: Open your account menu at the bottom of the sidebar, then choose Theme.

items.title: Pick Light, Dark, or System
items.description: A check mark shows what's active. System follows your computer automatically.

items.title: Watch it switch
items.description: The new theme applies instantly, and Connex remembers it for next time.

blocks.title: Colors stay readable
blocks.body: When you switch themes, Connex retunes every color for the mode you're in, so text and badges keep good contrast in both light and dark.

items.title: Brand color
items.description: Connex green marks buttons, active items, and highlights, so you always know what you can act on.

items.title: Typography
items.description: Clean, readable type for everything you write and read, with a dedicated Japanese typeface when you switch languages.

items.title: Warmth colors
items.description: Each relationship temperature, hot, warm, cool, and cold, has its own color and dot, so you can scan a list and know where things stand.

items.title: Chart colors
items.description: Charts use a consistent set of colors, with clear distinctions for won, lost, and open deals.

blocks.title: Prefer less movement?
blocks.body: If you've turned on reduced motion on your device, Connex skips its animations and simply shows you the result.

language-and-i18n.title: Language & internationalization
language-and-i18n.description: Switch between English and Japanese anywhere.

text: Connex speaks both English and Japanese, and it's a full translation, not just a few labels. Switch languages and the entire app changes, including dates and messages.
You can change the language from the sign-in pages or from inside the app, and your choice sticks the next time you come back.

items.title: Open the language switcher
items.description: Look for the globe icon. It shows your current language and lists English and Japanese.

items.title: Choose a language
items.description: A check mark shows what's active. The page refreshes for a moment while it applies.

items.title: Carry on
items.description: The whole app reappears in your chosen language.

blocks.title: Your choice is remembered
blocks.body: Connex saves your language, so it stays the same after a refresh or when you close and reopen your browser.

blocks.title: Fonts follow your language
blocks.body: You never have to pick a font. When you switch to Japanese, Connex automatically brings in a typeface made for Japanese text, so it looks right without any extra step.

items.title: Theming and appearance
items.description: How themes, colors, and typography come together across the app.

blocks.text: You can drive Connex from the keyboard. Search, menus, dropdowns, and dialogs all respond to keys, so you can move around without reaching for the mouse.

items.action: Move through search results or a menu
Open the highlighted result or confirm a choice
Close the open search, menu, or dialog

blocks.text: The search bar is a fast way to jump anywhere. Start typing and it searches across everything in your workspace, including companies, contacts, deals, tags, notes, tasks, and files, and groups the results by type so they're easy to scan.

blocks.title: Type two letters to start
blocks.body: Search waits until you've typed at least two characters, so a single keystroke doesn't flood the list. Arrow up and down to move through results, and the highlighted one scrolls into view on its own.

items.title: Menus
items.description: Arrow keys move through items, Enter or Space picks one, and Escape closes.

items.title: Searchable dropdowns
items.description: Type to filter long lists, pick one or several, and clear your choice in a click.

items.title: Clear focus
items.description: Wherever you are on the keyboard, a green ring shows which button or field is selected.

blocks.title: Works with screen readers
blocks.body: Connex is built to work with assistive technology, so screen readers can follow along as you move through the app.

tips-and-quirks.title: Tips & quirks
tips-and-quirks.description: Small behaviors and details that reward knowing.

blocks.text: Beyond the big features, Connex is full of small touches that make it feel considered. Here are a few worth knowing.

items.title: Edit your profile in place
items.description: Click the pencil to change your username, name, email, and picture, with helpful checks as you type.

items.title: Instant picture preview
items.description: Drop in a new photo and you see it right away. Close without saving and it's cleared.

items.title: Switch workspaces
items.description: Move between workspaces or create a new one from a dropdown that shows where you are and how many you belong to.

items.title: Workspace marker
items.description: Each workspace gets a small green square with its first letter, so you can recognize it at a glance.

blocks.title: Small touches
body: Your profile page greets you a little differently each time.
Try to save your profile without changing anything and Connex just tells you there's nothing to save, instead of doing needless work.

items.title: Unread badge
items.description: The bell shows how many unread notifications you have, and it updates on its own and the moment you come back to the tab.

items.title: Across all your workspaces
items.description: The count covers everything unread across every workspace you belong to, not just the one you're in.

items.title: Toasts
items.description: Short messages pop up at the top to confirm a success or flag a problem, then clear on their own.

items.title: Helpful form feedback
items.description: Errors show right under the field, buttons show a spinner while they work so you don't submit twice, and empty screens point you to the next step.

items.title: Show or hide the sidebar
items.description: Collapse the sidebar to focus. On mobile it slides over and closes when you move on.

items.title: Collapsible sections
items.description: Fold away parts of the sidebar you're not using.

items.title: Clear active page
items.description: The page you're on is highlighted, and features that aren't ready yet are dimmed.

blocks.title: Scrolling wide tables
blocks.body: In wide tables and card rows, hold the middle mouse button and drag to scroll sideways. Fading edges hint there's more to see.

items.question: Will Connex remember my workspace?
items.answer: Yes. It remembers the workspace you were last in, so you land right back there even after closing your browser.

DocsTutorials.title: Tutorials
DocsTutorials.description: Short, hands-on walkthroughs that take you through common tasks from start to finish.
DocsTutorials.lead: Learn by doing. Each tutorial walks you through one real task step by step, so you can follow along in your own workspace.

add-your-first-company.title: Add your first company and contact
add-your-first-company.description: Create a company, add a person who works there, and open their profile.

blocks.text: This tutorial gets you from an empty workspace to your first real relationship in a few minutes. You will create a company, add a person who works there, and open their profile to see everything Connex starts tracking for you. It is the foundation everything else builds on, so it is the perfect place to begin.

blocks.name: contact-card
blocks.caption: A contact card, ready with their name, title, company, and warmth at a glance.

items.title: Open the new company form
items.description: Head to your Companies list and choose to add a company. A clean form opens, ready for you to fill in.

items.title: Enter the name and website
items.description: Type the company name and its website. The website field tidies up the address format for you, and the industry field suggests values you already use.

items.title: Save
items.description: The company is created right away. If you do not add a logo, Connex shows a friendly lettered avatar in its place.

blocks.title: Add the person at the same time
blocks.body: The new company form lets you line up its people while you are there. You can add a contact with a name, title, email, and photo, and Connex creates the company first, then the person. If you would rather do it as a separate step, follow the next section.

items.title: Start with a name
items.description: Open the company you just created and add a contact from its people section. The name is all you truly need to get started.

items.title: Fill in email and title
items.description: Add their work email and job title so you can reach them and remember who they are. These are optional, but they make the profile far more useful.

items.title: Save
items.description: A quick success animation confirms it and the form closes. The person is now linked to the company, and their current role is recorded in their work history automatically.

blocks.title: Open the profile and see what you get

items.title: Their details
items.description: Name, title, company, email, and phone laid out in a clean, easy-to-read profile you can edit anytime.

items.title: Tags
items.description: Add color-coded labels like prospect or champion to keep people organized and easy to filter later.

items.title: Warmth
items.description: A color-coded temperature pill shows how warm the relationship is and how many days before it starts to cool.

items.title: Timeline
items.description: A dated feed where every call, email, meeting, note, and task you log will appear from now on.

items.question: Do I have to fill in every field?
items.answer: No. A company needs only a name, and a person needs only a name. You can always come back and add the website, email, title, and more whenever you like.

items.question: Does the work history update itself?
items.answer: Yes. When you add a person to a company or move them later, Connex records the change for you and marks their current role, so their history stays accurate on its own.

items.title: Contacts
items.description: Everything a person's profile holds, from work history to connections.

items.title: Log a meeting and watch warmth rise
items.description: Record your first interaction and see the relationship warm up.

log-activity-and-warmth.title: Log a meeting and watch warmth rise
log-activity-and-warmth.description: Record an interaction and see how it lifts a relationship's temperature.

blocks.text: Just had a good meeting or a great call? Log it in Connex and you get two things at once: a tidy record of what happened, and a relationship that stays warm. This tutorial walks you through logging one interaction on a contact, then shows you where that shows up in their warmth score.

items.title: Open the contact
items.description: Go to Records, find the person you just spoke with, and click their name to open their profile.

items.title: Start a new activity
items.description: Choose Log activity on their profile. This is how you record a real touchpoint against them.

items.title: Pick the type
items.description: Select Meeting or Call. Each type carries its own color and icon, so your timeline stays easy to scan later.

items.title: Add a subject, time, and note
items.description: Give it a short title, set when it happened, and write a quick note with what was said or what to do next. The detail is what makes it worth looking back on.

items.title: Link it and save
items.description: The activity is already tied to this contact. Attach a deal too if it belongs to one, then save. It lands right on their history.

blocks.text: Watch the warmth respond

You never set warmth by hand. Connex reads it from the things you log: your calls, meetings, notes, and follow-ups. The moment your activity is saved, it counts as recent, meaningful contact, and the relationship's warmth ticks upward. You will see it on the contact's profile as a color-coded temperature pill with a score and the days left before it starts to cool.

blocks.name: warmth-scale
blocks.caption: The four warmth bands, from thriving Hot down to quiet Cold.

blocks.title: Log while it is fresh
blocks.body: Jot the activity down right after the meeting, while the details are still in your head. A one-line note today is far more useful than a perfect memory you never get around to writing. And every touchpoint you log keeps that relationship from cooling off.

items.title: Warmth & temperature
items.description: What each band means and how the score keeps itself current.

items.title: Activities
items.description: All your calls, meetings, and touchpoints in one timeline.

build-your-pipeline.title: Build a pipeline and move a deal
build-your-pipeline.description: Set up stages and move a deal from first contact to won.

blocks.text: In this tutorial you will set up a pipeline with a few stages, add a deal to one of your companies, and walk it all the way from first contact to won. By the end you will have a clear, visual way to see every opportunity you are working and know exactly what to do next.

blocks.name: pipeline-board
blocks.caption: Your stages laid out left to right, with each deal sitting in the stage it has reached.

items.title: Create a new pipeline
items.description: Open Records, go to your pipelines, and create one. Give it a name that matches how you sell, like New Business or Renewals.

items.title: Add your stages
items.description: Stages are the steps a deal moves through, in order. A simple set works great to start: Lead, Meeting, Proposal, then Negotiation. You can rename or remove them anytime.

items.title: Mark a winning and a losing stage
items.description: Choose one stage as your winning stage and one as your losing stage. When a deal reaches either one, Connex closes it with that outcome for you.

blocks.title: Add a deal and move it forward

items.title: Create a deal on a company
items.description: Add a new deal and link it to the company it belongs to. Give it a name so you can spot it at a glance.

items.title: Set the value and currency
items.description: The value is what the opportunity is worth to you. Enter the amount and its currency, so your forecasts and totals add up correctly.

items.title: Move it through your stages
items.description: As things progress, move the deal into its next stage. The deal's page shows a timeline of its stages, with the current one highlighted, so you always know where it stands.

items.title: Mark it won
items.description: When you land it, move the deal into your winning stage. It closes as won on its own, the close date fills in for you, and you can record the value you actually landed.

blocks.title: Let the winning stage do the work
blocks.body: You do not have to close a deal by hand. Just drag it into the stage you marked as winning and Connex records the win, fills in the close date, and updates your forecast. The same goes for your losing stage when a deal does not work out.

items.question: What is the difference between a stage and the value?
items.answer: A stage is where a deal is in your process, like Proposal or Negotiation. The value is how much money the deal is worth. Stages tell you what to do next, and value tells you what is at stake.

items.question: Can I reopen a deal I closed by mistake?
items.answer: Yes. Reopen it and Connex clears the close date and outcome and moves it off the closing stage, so the deal is active again.

items.title: Deals & pipelines
items.description: A fuller tour of stages, currencies, collaborators, and the deals dashboard.

items.title: Companies
items.description: Organize the organizations your deals belong to, with their people and history.

request-a-warm-intro.title: Find and request a warm introduction
request-a-warm-intro.description: See who can introduce you to someone, and ask for the intro.

blocks.text: The warmest way to reach someone new is through a person you both trust. In this tutorial you will open the Introductions tool, find a warm path between two people in your network, and make the introduction. By the end you will know how to spot the strongest connector for any pairing and record the intro so it becomes part of your history.

blocks.name: warm-intro-path
blocks.caption: A warm path from you to the person you want to reach, through someone you both know.

blocks.text: A warm path is simply the chain of trust that gets you to someone. Instead of a cold message to a stranger, Connex looks at the people you already know and finds pairs you are perfectly placed to introduce, because you know both of them but they do not yet know each other. Each suggested pair comes with a match strength and a short reason, so you can see at a glance why it is a good introduction to make.

items.title: Open the Introductions page
items.description: Head to Introductions in your overview area. You can also open it from the introduction opportunities shown on your dashboard, which link straight through to this page.

items.title: Review your intros to make
items.description: Under Intros to make you will see pairs of people you are well placed to connect. Each one is someone your team has actually engaged with, so every suggestion is a person you can credibly introduce.

items.title: Read the warm path
items.description: Every suggestion shows a match strength, either Strong, Good, or Fair, along with a short reason such as shared connections or a shared employer. That reason is the warm path itself, the honest answer to why these two belong together.

items.title: Search for a specific person
items.description: Looking to connect two people who were not suggested? Choose Log an intro, then search your contacts to pick the first person and the second person by name.

items.title: Make the introduction and record it
items.description: Once you have made the intro, select Record intro. Connex connects the two people and adds the introduction to your history.

blocks.title: Dismiss the pairs that do not fit
blocks.body: If a suggested pair is not right, choose Dismiss. It sets the pair aside without recording anything and quietly steers future suggestions toward better matches. Dismissing only affects pairs you have not introduced yet, so your history stays accurate and is never rewritten.

items.question: Where do these suggestions come from?
items.answer: They are drawn from people you actually stay in touch with, matched on things like shared connections or a shared employer. Pairs who already know each other, or that you have recorded or dismissed before, are left out.

items.question: Can I introduce two people who were not suggested?
items.answer: Yes. Use Log an intro to record an introduction between any two contacts, even one Connex never surfaced, with an optional note.

items.question: What if I introduce the same two people twice?
items.answer: Nothing gets duplicated. Recording the same pairing again just updates the existing entry, and once an intro is recorded it stays recorded, so your history stays tidy.

items.title: Warm-intro paths
items.description: A deeper look at how Connex finds the strongest path to any person.

items.title: Relationship map
items.description: See the connection map these suggestions are drawn from, laid out for you to explore.

import-your-contacts.title: Import your existing contacts
import-your-contacts.description: Bring contacts in from a spreadsheet in a few guided steps.

blocks.text: Already have your contacts in a spreadsheet? This tutorial walks you through bringing them into Connex in a few guided steps. You line up your columns, look over a preview of exactly what will happen, and only then confirm, so nothing gets created or changed until you say so.

blocks.name: import-wizard
blocks.caption: Matching your spreadsheet columns to Connex fields

blocks.title: Import your contacts step by step

items.title: Start the import
items.description: Open your Contacts and select Import. A friendly step-by-step wizard opens and walks you the rest of the way.

items.title: Choose your CSV file
items.description: Drop your spreadsheet onto the upload area, or click to browse for it. Save your file as CSV first, and keep it under 5,000 rows and 5MB. Connex reads it right away and shows you what it found.

items.title: Match your columns
items.description: Line up each column in your file with a field in Connex, like Name, Email, Phone, Title, or Company. Name is required. You can create a new field on the spot for anything that doesn't fit, or set a column to Ignore if you don't need it.

items.title: Review the preview
items.description: See exactly what will happen for every row before anything is saved. Each row is marked New, Match, Skip, or Invalid, so you can spot people you already have and catch any rows that need a fix.

items.title: Confirm the import
items.description: When the preview looks right, select Import. Connex creates and updates your contacts, then shows you how many were created, updated, and skipped.

blocks.title: Bring your tags and companies along
blocks.body: Add a column named 'tags' with several tags separated by commas, and any that don't exist yet are created for you. Add a 'company' column and Connex links each person to their company, creating the company if it's new. One tidy spreadsheet can set up a lot in a single pass.

items.question: Will importing overwrite my existing contacts?
items.answer: Only if you choose to. When a row matches someone you already have, you decide what happens: fill in just the blanks, skip the row, or overwrite with the new details. Nothing changes until you confirm.

items.question: What if some rows have errors?
items.answer: Rows marked Invalid in the preview aren't imported. The final step offers a download of just those rows with a note on what went wrong, so you can fix them and import again.

items.title: Import & export
items.description: The full guide to bringing records in from CSV and taking your data back out.

items.title: Contacts
items.description: See how the people you just imported come to life on their profiles.

DocsMarketing.title: Marketing
DocsMarketing.description: Campaigns, audiences, and the delivery rules Connex applies on your behalf.
DocsMarketing.lead: Connex can send an email or SMS campaign to a frozen audience of your contacts. The rules around consent, frequency, and measurement are deliberately conservative, and this section is honest about what is and is not counted.

campaigns.title: Campaigns
campaigns.description: Build an audience, freeze it, attach a message, and send.

text: A campaign is a piece of outreach to a group of your contacts. You describe who it is for, freeze that group so it can never shift underneath you, attach a message, and send it. Everything is scoped to your workspace, and only people who have not opted out are ever contacted.
Campaigns live under Marketing in the sidebar.

blocks.name: campaign-flow
blocks.caption: An audience becomes a frozen snapshot before a message is ever attached to it.

items.title: Create the campaign
items.description: Give it a name, an objective, a type and a status. You can also record a budget and a start and end date for your own reference. These are set once here and cannot be changed afterwards, so take a moment over the status in particular.

items.title: Build the audience
items.description: Use the segment builder to describe who should receive it. Estimate the audience to see how many people are included, and how many were left out because of consent, suppression, or a processing restriction.

items.title: Freeze a snapshot
items.description: Freezing captures the audience as a numbered version. Sends always run against a frozen snapshot, so the group cannot change between the moment you review it and the moment it goes out.

items.title: Write a message
items.description: Add a message for the email or SMS channel, then add a revision with the subject and body. Revisions are added, never edited or removed, so you always keep the exact wording that went out.

items.title: Create and queue the send
items.description: Pick a frozen snapshot version and a message revision, then queue it. Queued sends go out on the next delivery pass. You can pause or cancel a send while it is running. Sends cannot be scheduled for a later time: queueing is what sends them.

blocks.title: Sending has to be switched on for the whole instance
blocks.body: Campaigns are visible to everyone, but delivering them depends on two separate instance-level settings your administrator controls, and both are off unless they turn them on. One allows a send to be queued at all; the other allows queued sends to actually go out. With only the first enabled, queueing appears to succeed and nothing is ever delivered, so ask your administrator to confirm both. Until it is on, you can build campaigns, audiences and messages normally, and queueing a send is refused with a message saying so. A working email or SMS transport also has to be configured before a send can be queued.

items.title: Only people, and only the willing
items.description: Only person audiences can be sent to. Anyone who has unsubscribed, been suppressed, or had processing restricted is excluded, and the estimate tells you how many that was.

items.title: One message per person per day
items.description: A person receives at most one message on a channel in any 24 hours, counted across campaigns. Anyone caught by that cap is reported as skipped rather than silently dropped.

items.title: Unsubscribes are automatic
items.description: Connex gives every recipient their own unsubscribe token, but it only reaches them if the message body includes the unsubscribe placeholder, so put it in every template you write. Unsubscribing suppresses that person and withdraws consent immediately, and it applies to future campaigns too.

items.title: Bounces and complaints suppress
items.description: When your email provider reports a hard bounce or a spam complaint, Connex suppresses that address and revokes consent without anyone having to act. This needs an email provider that sends those reports back; on a plain mail server no such report ever arrives and nothing is suppressed.

blocks.title: Opens and clicks are never tracked
blocks.body: Connex does not put a tracking pixel in your email and does not rewrite your links. That is a deliberate choice, not a missing feature, so there are no open or click figures anywhere and there never will be from Connex itself.

blocks.title: What the engagement figures mean
rows: Connex itself, as it hands each message to your transport. Always available.
People using the unsubscribe link in a message you sent.
Receipts reported back by your email provider. These need a provider that sends receipts, otherwise they read as not measured rather than zero.

items.question: Can I change a campaign after I create it?
items.answer: Not from the campaign screens. Treat the name, objective, type, status, budget and dates as decisions you make once, because the create dialog is your only chance to set them. Status is the one that catches people out, since it looks like something you would advance as the campaign progresses. Audiences, messages and sends are the parts you keep working on.

items.question: Why did far fewer people receive it than my audience showed?
items.answer: Check the skip reasons on the send. The usual causes are people with no address on that channel, the one-message-per-day cap, or consent and suppression.

items.question: Is the Exports tab a download?
items.answer: No. It pushes a frozen audience to an external list service your administrator has connected. Nothing is downloaded to your computer.

items.title: Saved views and segments
items.description: The same segment rules you use to build a campaign audience.

items.description: Why your mail lands in an inbox, and what Connex does and does not do about it.

DocsOperations.title: Running Connex
DocsOperations.description: What ships today, how Connex is deployed, where the boundaries sit, and how support works.
DocsOperations.lead: This section is for the people who have to trust Connex, not just use it. It sets out plainly what is finished and what is still early, how the different deployment shapes differ, what Connex can and cannot reach, and how to get help when something breaks.

what-connex-is-today.title: What Connex is today
what-connex-is-today.description: An honest picture of the product's scope, maturity, and intended use.

text: Connex is a relationship-intelligence CRM. It keeps companies, contacts and deals, scores how warm each relationship is, warns you when one is cooling, and works out the friendliest route to an introduction. On top of that sit reports, documents, campaigns and a set of optional AI features.
This page describes the state of the product rather than how to use it. If you are evaluating Connex, or you are responsible for it inside your organisation, start here.

items.title: One workspace, one boundary
items.description: Every record, file, tag and setting belongs to exactly one workspace and never appears in another. That separation is enforced in the database layer, not just in the interface.

items.title: Deterministic figures first
items.description: Warmth, risk, pipeline and report figures are computed from your data by rules you can reason about. Where AI is involved it explains those figures, it does not produce them.

items.title: Fail closed
items.description: When a check cannot be completed, Connex refuses rather than guesses. Optional features generally stay hidden when they are not configured, rather than appearing and then failing. Campaign delivery says so in place rather than hiding, because the rest of the campaign surface still works without it.

items.title: Japanese as a first language
items.description: The whole interface, and this documentation, ship in Japanese and English. Japanese is not an afterthought translation layer.

blocks.title: Connex is pre-1.0
blocks.body: Some surfaces are complete and in daily use, some are deliberately switched off until an external gate clears, and a few exist as groundwork for later work. The next article says exactly which is which, per surface, so you never have to guess from the interface alone.

blocks.text: Connex is designed to be run in more than one shape: as a service operated by Connex, as a dedicated environment operated by Connex for one customer, or entirely inside your own infrastructure. Which shape you are on changes who holds the keys and who can reach the data, and it is worth knowing which one you have.

items.description: A surface-by-surface status list, including everything that is off by default.

whats-shipped-and-whats-preview.title: What ships and what is preview
whats-shipped-and-whats-preview.description: A surface-by-surface status list, including everything that is off unless an administrator turns it on.

text: Connex ships a lot of surfaces, and several of them are switched off out of the box. A feature being off does not always look different in the interface, so this page states the status of each one plainly.

Three separate things have to line up before an optional feature works: your deployment shape has to allow it, your administrator has to configure it, and you have to hold the right permission. Any one of them missing is usually enough to make a feature unavailable, though Campaigns is an exception worth knowing: without permission to view campaigns the menu entry still appears and the list simply looks empty.

blocks.title: Core CRM
rows: Shipped and on. No configuration needed.
Tags, files, saved views and segments
Search, filters, bulk actions, custom fields
Shipped and on. Products are export only, with no import.
Shipped and on. Managing the catalogue is an administrator permission.
Shipped and on. Scheduled delivery needs working email.
Shipped and on. A read-only health page for your workspace, and an organisation-wide view for administrators.
Shipped and on. An organisation administrator can download a redacted diagnostic bundle to hand to support.

blocks.title: Off unless an administrator turns it on
rows: Off by default for the whole instance. Also needs your organisation to connect its own AI provider, and the permission is administrator-only by default.
Off by default. The campaign screens are visible either way; only sending is refused.
Off by default. Supports OpenID Connect and SAML.
Off by default, and ships with no credentials.

Depends on whether card reading is enabled for your instance.
Depends on your deployment shape. Not available on a self-hosted deployment, where you configure your own mail.
Off by default. People normally join an existing workspace by invitation.

blocks.title: Connected account capture is an internal preview
blocks.body: Reading your mailbox and calendar to capture relationship signals is built and works, but it is not generally available. It stays behind provider verification that is still in progress, and it should not be switched on for production use until that clears. Connecting an account is separate, and does not start any capture on its own.

blocks.title: Where a feature is off, it usually just is not there
blocks.body: Connex hides what it cannot deliver rather than showing a control that fails. That means an absent panel is often the correct signal that something is not configured, rather than a fault. There are two exceptions, and both announce themselves in place. Reports always render their figures, and only the written summary reports itself as unavailable. Campaigns keep their planning, audience and message screens live whether or not sending is enabled, because those genuinely work without it; the delivery and export panels say up front when sending is not enabled on this instance, and the queue control stays disabled.

deployment-profiles.title: Deployment shapes
deployment-profiles.description: The three ways Connex runs, and what changes between them.

blocks.text: Every Connex deployment declares which shape it is. That declaration is required, and an instance that does not set it refuses to start rather than guessing. The shape decides who operates the environment, who holds the keys, and which settings are allowed at all.

blocks.name: deployment-profiles
blocks.caption: The three shapes differ mainly in who operates the environment and holds the keys.

blocks.title: The three shapes
rows: A shared, hardened environment run by Connex. The internal escape hatches an operator might use in their own network are refused outright.
Your own environment with its own database, still operated by Connex on your behalf.
Connex runs entirely inside your infrastructure. You control the network, you generate and hold the keys, and Connex operates nothing.

items.title: Who can reach the environment
items.description: On a self-hosted deployment, Connex has no remote access to your instance and nothing reports back to Connex. On a Connex-operated shape, Connex staff operate the environment under the terms of your agreement.

items.title: Who holds the keys
items.description: A self-hosted deployment generates and holds its own encryption and audit-integrity secrets, and they never leave your environment. A Connex-operated shape is operated by Connex, so it does not carry that guarantee.

items.title: Which mail path is available
items.description: Connex-managed email is only possible where Connex operates the environment. A self-hosted deployment configures its own mail server, and enabling managed mail there is refused at startup rather than quietly ignored.

items.title: Which optional features are permitted
items.description: Almost every optional feature is available in every shape and gated only by your administrator's configuration. Managed email is the single exception that a shape forbids outright.

blocks.title: Permitted is not the same as enabled
blocks.body: Your deployment shape only decides what is allowed. A feature still has to be configured by your administrator and granted to you before you can use it, so a capability being permitted in your shape tells you nothing about whether it is switched on.

items.description: What Connex can reach, and how support works without that access.
